gui.xaero_old_minecraft: This feature is not available on this old version of Minecraft.

gui.xaero_howto_select: Left-click an interface to select it.
gui.xaero_howto_drag: Left-click and drag to move an interface around.
gui.xaero_howto_center: Press "C" to center or uncenter the selected interface.
gui.xaero_different_centered: Some interfaces have a different centered look.
gui.xaero_howto_flip: Press "F" to flip or unflip the selected interface.
gui.xaero_howto_settings: Press "S" to quickly access settings of the selected interface.
gui.xaero_howto_preset: Select a preset by clicking the "Choose a Preset" button.
gui.xaero_howto_save: Save your changes by clicking the "Confirm" button.
gui.xaero_howto_cancel: Discard your changes by clicking the "Cancel" button.
gui.xaero_server_disabled: The server might have disabled some of the mod features.
gui.xaero_minimap_guide: Left-click and drag to move the minimap around.
gui.xaero_clear_set_message: Are you sure you would like to clear the current set
gui.xaero_clear_set_message2: All waypoints from this set will be deleted!
gui.xaero_delete_set_message: Are you sure you would like to delete the current set
gui.xaero_delete_set_message2: This set will be removed from the current world.
gui.xaero_reset_message: Are you sure you would like to restore the default settings?
gui.xaero_safe_mode_box: Use Java-based (CPU) equivalent of this mod instead of the default, OpenGL-based (GPU) one. Safe mode is a plan B in case the mod does not function correctly. Not all features work in the safe mode. Do not use unless you have to.
gui.xaero_make_automatic_msg2: This will swap all waypoint data between the selected world/server and the auto one, thus simulate making the selected world/server automatic. Make sure you know what you are doing.
gui.xaero_make_multi_automatic_msg2: This will swap all waypoint data between the selected sub-world and the auto one, thus simulate making the selected sub-world automatic. Make sure you know what you are doing.
gui.xaero_delete_world_msg1: Would you like to delete all waypoint data for the selected world/server?
gui.xaero_delete_world_msg2: This action cannot be undone! Make sure you know what you are doing.
gui.xaero_delete_multi_world_msg1: Would you like to delete all waypoint data for the selected sub-world?
gui.xaero_delete_multi_world_msg2: This action cannot be undone! Make sure you know what you are doing.
gui.xaero_multiply_msg1: This option should be used only to fix incorrect waypoint coordinates.
gui.xaero_multiply_msg2: Are you sure you would like to MULTIPLY all sub-world coordinates by 8?
gui.xaero_divide_msg2: Are you sure you would like to DIVIDE all sub-world coordinates by 8?
gui.xaero_share_msg1: Are you sure you would like to share this waypoint with EVERYONE in the chat?
gui.xaero_share_msg2: Make sure you do not expose a secret location!
gui.xaero_visit_needed: You need to visit this dimension first to convert it to the new format!
gui.xaero_teleportation_tooltip: Once disabled, it can be enabled back only through the config file!
gui.xaero_use_multiworld_tooltip: Disable if this is a simple server with a single world (no separate lobby, game mode, or minigame worlds). Multiworld detection will cause only issues on such servers. However, installing this mod on the server side should prevent these issues.
gui.xaero_box_cave_maps: Mapping mode that can go deeper than the surface blocks, mainly to display underground caves and interiors of buildings. The ceiling size refers to the size of a horizontal "square" of solid blocks that has to be detected above you to activate the cave mode.
gui.xaero_box_cave_maps2: Mapping mode that can go deeper than the surface blocks, mainly to display underground caves and interiors of buildings. The ceiling size refers to the size of a square ceiling of solid blocks that has to be detected above you to activate the cave mode. The solid blocks don't have to be on the same Y level.
gui.xaero_box_entity_amount: The limit per each entity category.
gui.xaero_box_distance: Specifies, for which in-world waypoints to show the distance to.
gui.xaero_box_distance2: Specifies, for which in-world waypoints to show the distance to. This does not guarantee that it will be shown for multiple waypoints at once. Check out the "Multiple Waypoint Distances" setting as well.
gui.xaero_box_always_distance: Display distance even when the waypoint is very close. This setting does not override the "Distance to WP" option.
gui.xaero_box_arrow_scale: Scale of the arrow used in the non-rotating variant of the minimap and several other cases.
gui.xaero_box_arrow_color: Color of the arrow used in the non-rotating variant of the minimap and several other cases.
gui.xaero_box_cave_zoom: Specifies, how much to zoom the minimap further in when the cave mode is active.
gui.xaero_box_entity_depth: Display entities darker on the minimap depending on their Y level relative to you.
gui.xaero_box_height_limit: Maximum Y-level distance for entities until they are no longer displayed on the minimap.
gui.xaero_box_always_entity_nametags: Always render names for entities with name tags regardless of what the name setting is set to in the "Entity Radar" screen.
gui.xaero_box_teleport_default_command: The command used for waypoint teleportation if a world-specific or a server-specific command is not set in the Options menu in the waypoint screen.
gui.xaero_teleport_coordinates_hidden: Unable to teleport, because it would expose the waypoint coordinates. Disable the "Hide Waypoint Coordinates" option to be able to freely teleport again.
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_distance: Maximum render distance for local waypoints. Global waypoints are not affected.
gui.xaero_world_connection_tooltip: Connect/disconnect selected sub-world to/from the current auto one. Connect only sub-worlds that are from the same sub-server/world save. For example, if a vanilla Nether portal takes you from sub-world A to sub-world B, then you can safely connect them. Other sub-worlds connected to the current one are always at the top of the list and are marked by an asterisk (symbol: *).
gui.xaero_connect_with_auto_msg: Would you like to create the following connection between sub-worlds?
gui.xaero_disconnect_from_auto_msg: Would you like to delete the following connection between sub-worlds?
gui.xaero_teleport_not_connected: You are trying to teleport to a sub-world that is not connected to the current auto one. If you are sure that this sub-world is from the same sub-server/world save as the auto one, then you can enable teleportation by adding a connection in the waypoint screen -> Options -> Add Sub-World Connection. But beware, if you connect unrelated sub-worlds and teleport, then there is a good chance you will suffocate in a block or die from fall damage, so be careful and connect only the right ones.
gui.xaero_box_ignore_heightmaps: Some servers put custom values in the world heightmaps, which may result in incorrectly rendered maps. Sometimes it may even happen in heavily modded singleplayer worlds. This option should fix such issues at the expense of a bit of performance. Do not use unless you have to. Reenter the world after toggling this option! Stored per world/server, not part of the config profile.
gui.xaero_error_loading_properties: Error loading server minimap properties. Please retry.
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_bottom: Put newly created waypoints at the bottom of the waypoint list instead of the default top.
gui.xaero_box_entity_radar_names:
Render entity names under the dots or icons/heads. 
 
 Option "Player List" - render only when the "List Players" key binding (TAB by default) is pressed.
gui.xaero_box_light_overlay_type: Using this overlay can negatively affect the game performance because it currently does not use the World Map mod chunks and increases the minimap updating frequency. Do not keep it active all the time.
gui.xaero_box_entity_radar_icons:
Render entity icons instead of colored dots. 
 
 Option "Player List" - render only when the "List Players" key binding (TAB by default) is pressed.
gui.xaero_box_minimap_size:
Size of the minimap frame that affects how much is visible. Square-shaped minimap is forced into the non-rotating mode (option "Lock Minimap North") when the size is greater than 180. 
 
 For the "Auto" option, go all the way to the left. 
 
 Size values in older mod versions: 
 Tiny - 57 
 Small - 85 
 Medium - 113 
 Large - 169
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_clamp_depth:
The screen depth at which in-world waypoints stop getting smaller when you go further away from them. 
 Use this if you want to make waypoints that are far away bigger/smaller on the screen. Use the "Waypoint In-World Scale" setting to also affect the size of waypoints when you are close to them. 
 
 For the "Auto" option, go all the way to the left. 
 The automatic option attempts to give you the best value for the default values of scale types, taking your FOV and screen height into account. 
 
 Default values in older mod versions: 
 Clamp Depth: 12 
 In-World Scale: 2.5 
 Name Text Scale: 0.5 
 Distance Text Scale: 0.8
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_distance_scale:
Scale of the text displaying the distance to a waypoint in world. 
 
 Default values in older mod versions: 
 Clamp Depth: 12 
 In-World Scale: 2.5 
 Name Text Scale: 0.5 
 Distance Text Scale: 0.8
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_name_scale:
Scale of the text displaying the name of a waypoint in world. 
 
 Default values in older mod versions: 
 Clamp Depth: 12 
 In-World Scale: 2.5 
 Name Text Scale: 0.5 
 Distance Text Scale: 0.8
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_scale:
Scale of waypoints in world. Use this to change the scale of all waypoints in world, including those that are near you. Use the "Clamp Depth" setting to specifically affect the size of waypoints that are far away. 
 
 Default values in older mod versions: 
 Clamp Depth: 12 
 In-World Scale: 2.5 
 Name Text Scale: 0.5 
 Distance Text Scale: 0.8
gui.xaero_uses_worldmap_value: Setting value is taken from the world map settings!
gui.xaero_uses_worldmap_hard_value: Setting value cannot be configured when using the world map chunks!
gui.xaero_box_ui_scale: Scale of text and other minimap UI elements. Not made for zooming in or resizing. There are separate options for that.
gui.xaero_box_pushbox_boss_health:
An invisible box around the vanilla boss health display that pushes the mod's interfaces out of the way. 
 
 Normal type's collision box is equal to its size and only pushes interfaces by the necessary distance. 
 
 Screen Height type's collision box is stretched across the whole screen height and always shifts colliding interfaces vertically by the Normal type's height. This can be very useful when you have multiple interfaces in a column and want all of them to be pushed.
gui.xaero_box_pushbox_potion_effects:
An invisible box around the vanilla potion effects display that pushes the mod's interfaces out of the way. 
 
 Normal type's collision box is equal to its size and only pushes interfaces by the necessary distance. 
 
 Screen Height type's collision box is stretched across the whole screen height and always shifts colliding interfaces vertically by the Normal type's height. This can be very useful when you have multiple interfaces in a column and want all of them to be pushed.
gui.xaero_box_minimap_frame_color: The color of the minimap frame for the non-default colored frame styles.
gui.xaero_box_compass_scale: The scale of the compass letters NESW when using the on-map compass location.
gui.xaero_box_compass_over_wp2: Render compass letters (N, E, S, W) over the on-map waypoints. This only works for the on-frame compass location.
gui.xaero_teleport_y_unknown: You can't teleport to a waypoint that doesn't specify the Y coordinate. Edit the waypoint to be able to teleport to it.
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_distance_scale2: Scale of the text displaying the distance to a waypoint in world.
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_name_scale2: Scale of the text displaying the name of a waypoint in world.
gui.xaero_box_ingame_waypoint_icon_scale: Scale of the waypoint icons in world.
gui.xaero_box_ingame_waypoint_close_scal: Scale of the waypoints in world when you are very close to them. To change the scale of waypoints that are far away, use the "In-World Waypoint Icon Scale", "Waypoint Distance Text Scale" and "Waypoint Name Text Scale" settings.
gui.xaero_box_multiple_waypoint_info: Whether the distance can be displayed for multiple waypoints in world at once. By default, only the distance to the closest waypoint to the crosshair is displayed. Use the "Distance to WP" setting to configure which waypoints the distance could even be shown for.
gui.xaero_box_category_include_list2: A list of entities to include in the (sub-)category on top of the entities included by the "Hard Include".
gui.xaero_box_category_exclude_list2: A list of entities to exclude from the entities already included in the (sub-)category. Can work both as a "whitelist" and a "blacklist" depending on the exclusion mode you choose. This does not remove entities from the entity radar, unless you're excluding from the root "Any" category. The "Display" setting can remove entities from the radar.
gui.xaero_box_category_hard_include2: Controls which entities to automatically include in the (sub-)category without having to put them in the include list manually.
gui.xaero_category_disable_protection_co: Disable protection for the following category?
gui.xaero_category_enable_protection_con: Enable protection for the following category?
gui.xaero_box_category_protection: Category protection prevents you from (accidentally) deleting, moving, renaming a category or changing its "Hard Include" setting.
gui.xaero_category_settings_reset_confir: Reset the category configuration to default values?
Custom categories will be removed and the default ones will be reset.
gui.xaero_box_radar_render_order: Controls the order in which the radar categories are rendered. A lower number means being rendered earlier. However, in the newer Minecraft versions dots are always rendered on top of the icons. The order still applies within dot or icon rendering though.
gui.xaero_box_always_entity_nametags2: Always render names for entities with name tags regardless of what the name setting is set to.
narration.xaero_ui_list_left_right_usage: Press LEFT and RIGHT buttons to select a column within the entry.
gui.xaero_category_help2:
Select a sub-category and go to its Settings to configure things like dot color, names, icons etc. 
 
 Sub-categories that are higher on the list are prioritized when multiple sub-categories include the same entity! Keep that in mind when creating custom categories. Usually, a new custom category should be placed at the top.
gui.xaero_box_adjust_height_for_carpetli: Subtract 1 from the height value for short carpetlike blocks, e.g. carpet, 1-layer snow, lilypad etc. This prevents such blocks from causing harsh shading on the map like a full block.
gui.xaero_category_settings_save_confirm: Warning: This confirmation screen was recently replaced!
gui.xaero_start_fading_at: Min Y Distance For Depth Fade
gui.xaero_box_start_fading_at: Minimum Y level difference requirement for an entity to start darkening on the radar when the "Show Entity Depth" setting is enabled.
gui.xaero_partial_y_teleportation: Use Y With Partial When TP
gui.xaero_box_partial_y_teleportation: When teleporting to a waypoint, offset the Y coordinate by 0.5 to avoid falling through carpet-like blocks into the void. Otherwise, the integer Y coordinate is used.
gui.xaero_box_delete_reached_deathpoints: Automatically delete deathpoints when you are within 4 blocks from them. This requires the deathpoint to be visible in world or on the minimap. A deathpoint is protected from deletion for 5 seconds after its creation.
gui.xaero_box_hide_minimap_under_screen: Hide the minimap when a GUI screen is open, e.g. the inventory, with the exception of minimap-related screens and the chat screen.
gui.xaero_box_category_list_add:
Supports player names, entity/item identifiers or patterns with special characters * ) ( and |. 
 
 * - matches anything. 
 )( - parenthesis, mostly for usage with |. 
 | - the OR operator to match different sequences in the same location. 
 
 For example: 
 minecraft:creeper 
 minecraft:zombie(_villager|_horse) - zombie villagers and horses. 
 minecraft:a*l - any vanilla entity which starts with 'a' and ends with 'l'.
gui.xaero_box_hide_minimap_under_f3: Hide the minimap when the F3 debug screen is enabled.
gui.xaero_box_manual_cave_mode_start: Which Y level to start mapping blocks from when the manual cave mode is enabled. Manual cave mode can be toggled with a key binding. For the "Auto" option, go all the way to the left.
gui.xaero_box_radar_render_over_minimap:
Render the entities over the minimap frame instead of rendering them inside the frame. Entities rendered this way act similarly to the waypoints and stick to the border when out of bounds. Visible entities are still limited to the ones loaded on the game client side though. 
 
 Option "Player List" - render over minimap only when the "List Players" key binding (TAB by default) is pressed.
gui.xaero_box_compass_over_everything: Render the cardinal direction letters (N, E, S, W) above all map elements, as opposed to under some, e.g. waypoints.
gui.xaero_box_tracked_players: Display players whose locations are shared with you in one way or another (usually your party) when they are out of the minimap frame bounds or not visible for another reason.
gui.xaero_box_pac_claims: Display chunk claims from the Open Parties and Claims mod as a colored overlay.
gui.xaero_box_pac_claims_border_opacity: The opacity of the chunk claims overlay border color. Chunk claims require the Open Parties and Claims mod.
gui.xaero_box_pac_claims_fill_opacity: The opacity of the chunk claims overlay fill color. Chunk claims require the Open Parties and Claims mod.
gui.xaero_box_pac_current_claim: Display claim information about the chunk that you are in. Chunk claims require the Open Parties and Claims mod.
gui.xaero_box_category_include_list_incl: Automatically include all entities from this list, and other lists included in this category, in the super-category/parent of this category, except the entities in the exclude list. That way you don't have to manually add duplicates on each level.

Automatically include all elements from this list, and other sub-lists included in this category, in the super-category/parent of this category. That way you don't have to manually add duplicates on each level. Keep in mind that super-categories are not going to check the exclusion lists of this category.
gui.xaero_box_temp_waypoints_global: When enabled, temporary waypoints are treated as global waypoints and ignore the waypoint render distance limits.
gui.xaero_box_keep_enlarged_minimap_unlo: Do not lock the minimap to north when enlarged if possible, which is only when using the circle shape at the time of writing this.
gui.xaero_box_enlarged_minimap_a_toggle: Treat the "Enlarge Minimap" key binding as a toggle instead of having to hold it.
gui.xaero_box_visibility_type:
In-World/Minimap Visibility Type 
 
 Local - only visible when in the maximum waypoint render distance 
 Global - always visible 
 World Map Loc. - not visible but is considered local 
 World Map Glo. - not visible but is considered global
gui.xaero_option_requires_ingame: This option requires you to be in game.
gui.xaero_box_switch_to_auto_on_death: Whether to switch the waypoint sub-world to auto on deathpoint creation. This doesn't affect what sub-world the deathpoint is created in.
gui.xaero_minimap_info_display_manager_h: Click and drag the elements to change the order of the displayed information.
gui.xaero_box_info_display_background_op: The opacity of the colored backgrounds of information types that have a background enabled in the info display manager.
gui.xaero_box_waypoint_type:
Enabled - regular waypoint 
 Disabled - regular hidden waypoint 
 Temporary - waypoint disappears on world exit 
 Destination - waypoint disappears when reached
gui.xaero_box_cave_mode_toggle_timer: The minimum time to wait between toggles of cave mode to prevent flickering when quickly switching between being under blocks and not. The latest world map mod has a separate setting for this as well.
gui.xaero_box_legible_cave_maps: Use depth-based lighting in cave mode instead of actual block lighting, making it easier to mentally separate the different cave layers.
gui.xaero_uses_worldmap_screen_value: Setting value is taken from the world map screen!
gui.xaero_box_biome_blending: Smooth out biome color edges by sampling biome colors for multiple blocks for every block on the map. Turning this off can significantly improve performance when biome color calculation is modded to be much more heavyweight than vanilla.
gui.xaero_box_minimap_info_display_manag: Configure and/or rearrange different types of info displayed under the minimap, such as current coordinates, facing angles, dimension, biome, weather, light level, game time, real time and more.
gui.xaero_box_entity_radar_categories: Configure specific entity categories, which are usually players, hostile mobs, friendly mobs, items or other entities, separately instead of having the same configuration for every entity. You can even create your own custom categories for specific entity types.
gui.xaero_box_compass: The cardinal directions displayed on the minimap.
gui.xaero_box_compass_color: The color of the background/shadow under the cardinal directions displayed on the minimap.
gui.xaero_box_north_compass_color: The color of the background/shadow under the north cardinal direction displayed on the minimap.
gui.xaero_box_compass_scale2: The scale of the cardinal direction letters NESW. For the "Auto" option, go all the way to the left.
gui.xaero_box_dimension_scaled_max_waypo: Scale the maximum waypoint render distance by the current dimension's coordinate scale (e.g. 1/8 in the Nether).
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_distance2: Maximum render distance for local waypoints. Global waypoints are not affected. By default, the maximum distance is scaled by the current dimension's coordinate scale. You can toggle this with "Dimension-scaled Max WP Distance".
gui.xaero_box_tracked_players_on_map: Display markers on the minimap for players whose locations are shared with you in one way or another (usually your party) when they are out of the minimap frame bounds or not visible for another reason. The "common" config has an option "everyoneTracksEveryone" that enables tracking of every player.
gui.xaero_box_tracked_players_in_world: Display markers in the world for players whose locations are shared with you in one way or another (usually your party). The "common" config has an option "everyoneTracksEveryone" that enables tracking of every player.
gui.xaero_box_tracked_player_world_icon_: Scale of the tracked player icons in world.
gui.xaero_box_tracked_player_world_name_: Scale of the text displaying the name of a tracked player in world.
gui.xaero_box_tracked_player_minimap_ico: Scale of the tracked player icons on the minimap.
gui.xaero_minimap_redirect_item: Disabled because you're missing the configured required item in your hotbar: %1$s!
gui.xaero_box_minimap_item: The ID of an item required in the hotbar for the minimap and waypoints to function. Set it to "-" to have no item requirement.
gui.xaero_config_redirect_fairplay: Disabled by fair-play mode enforced by the server!
gui.xaero_config_redirect_safe_mode: This value cannot be modified when the minimap is in safe mode.
gui.xaero_box_teleport_default_command_r: The command used for waypoint teleportation with rotation if a world-specific or a server-specific command is not set in the Options menu in the waypoint screen.
gui.xaero_box_cave_mode_allowed_dimensio: A list of dimension IDs, separated by comas, where cave mode should work. If the list is empty (just []), cave mode works in every dimension.
gui.xaero_mm_box_auto_cave_mode: Enable cave mode automatically based on what's above you. The ceiling size refers to the size of a square ceiling of solid blocks that has to be detected above you to activate the cave mode. The solid blocks don't have to be on the same Y level.
gui.xaero_box_cave_mode_allowed: Mapping mode that can go deeper than the surface blocks, mainly to display underground caves and interiors of buildings. Cave mode is usually enabled automatically (see "Auto Cave Mode"), but can also be toggled manually with a key binding (see "Manual Cave Mode Start Y").
gui.xaero_reset_config_profile_default_m: Are you sure you want to restore the default values in the config profile?
This action cannot be undone! Non-profile options aren't affected.
gui.xaero_box_potion_effects: An interface displaying currently active potion effects.
gui.xaero_box_armour_status: An interface displaying info about your currently worn armor and item held at the time.
gui.xaero_box_sprint: Sprint by holding one single (configurable) key binding.
gui.xaero_box_sneak: Allows you to toggle your sneak ON/OFF and stay sneaking without having to hold anything.
gui.xaero_box_notifications: On-screen notifications for various things, such as low health value, low hunger value, low oxygen value, danger of explosion, and being shot by (an) arrow(s).
gui.xaero_box_xp: Gained or lost experience indicator flying across your screen.
gui.xaero_box_quick_use: Action-bar-like system of key bindings that lets you automatically use a specified item from your hotbar without having to switch away from your currently held item. Holding the key binding lets you keep using the item like if you were holding the right mouse button. For example: placing torches, TNT, throwing potions, eating food, drinking.
gui.xaero_box_minimap: A minimap displaying your nearest surroundings and entities.
gui.xaero_box_entity_info: An interface displaying information about the living entity that you are pointing at, including players.
text.entityculling.title: EntityCulling
ftbchunks.own_claimed_chunks_on_map: Show your own claimed chunks on map
ftbchunks.death_waypoint_autoremove_dist: If > 0, the closest deathpoint will be auto-removed if it is closer than this distance from you
ftbchunks.zoom_warning: Max zoom-out limited due to memory constraints
ftbchunks.minimap.show_player_when_unloc: Show player when not locked north
ftbchunks.minimap.proportional.tooltip:
When true, minimap size is proportional to 10%% of the screen width (modifiable by the Scale setting)
When false, it is a fixed size regardless of screen resolution
ftbchunks.no_server_mod: FTB Chunks requires mod on server!
ftbteamsconfig.ftbchunks.allow_fake_play:
Treat ALL fake players as allies of the team.
WARNING: Setting this to true could allow hostile players to access your claims via any fake player. Set this to false if you're unsure.
ftbteamsconfig.ftbchunks.allow_named_fak:
Treat these fake players as allies of the team.
WARNING: Adding entries here could allow hostile players to access your claims via those fake players. Leave this empty if you're unsure.
ftbteamsconfig.ftbchunks.allow_fake_play: Allow Fake Players by Player ID
Allows fake players which have the ID of a real player access to your claims, IF that real player would be permitted, either as ally or team member. Set this to true if you're unsure.
ftbteamsconfig.ftbchunks.allow_explosion: Should explosions be able to damage blocks in claimed areas?
ftbteamsconfig.ftbchunks.allow_mob_grief:
Should mobs be allowed to damage blocks in claimed areas?
Note: currently Endermen only; may include other mobs in future
Creeper explosions are protected against via "Allow Explosions"
ftbteamsconfig.ftbchunks.block_edit_and_: Used when blocks are being placed, broken, or interacted with
ftbteamsconfig.ftbchunks.block_edit_mode: Used when blocks are being placed or broken
ftbteamsconfig.ftbchunks.block_interact_: Used when blocks are right-clicked, e.g. opening a chest or flipping a lever
ftbteamsconfig.ftbchunks.nonliving_entit: Used when non-living entities (paintings, item frames etc.) are left-clicked
ftbteamsconfig.ftbchunks.location_mode.t: Controls who can see you on the map or minimap (outside the normal vanilla tracking range)
ftbteamsconfig.ftbchunks.claim_visibilit: Controls who can see your claims on the map or minimap
ftbchunks.fake_players.tooltip:
CHECK: check fake player access like any real player
DENY: never allow fake players
ALLOW: always allow fake players
ftbchunks.max_claimed_chunks.tooltip: This default can be overridden by the FTB Ranks 'ftbchunks.max_claimed` permission node.
ftbchunks.max_force_loaded_chunks.toolti: This default can be overridden by the FTB Ranks 'ftbchunks.max_force_loaded` permission node.
ftbchunks.chunk_load_offline.tooltip:
Fallback offline chunk loading behaviour for when
 'Forceloading Mode' is set to 'default'
ftbchunks.force_load_mode.tooltip:
NEVER: only allow chunk force-loading if the owning team has at least one online player
ALWAYS: always allow force-loading, even if no players are online
DEFAULT: allow force-loading IF the team has at least one player with the FTB Ranks 'ftbchunks.chunk_load_offline' permission,
 OR 'Allow Forceloading for Offline Players' is true.
ftbchunks.disable_protection.tooltip:
Useful for private servers where everyone is trusted
and claims are only used for force-loading
ftbchunks.ally_mode: Allow Player to Change Ally Settings
ftbchunks.ally_mode.tooltip:
DEFAULT: FTB Teams ally status is checked to decide if players are allied
FORCED_ALL: all players are always considered to be allied
FORCED_NONE: no players are ever considered to be allied
ftbchunks.claim_dimension_blacklist.tool:
List of dimension ID's where chunks may not be claimed.
E.g. add "minecraft:the_end" to this list to disable chunk claiming in The End
Wildcards are allowed, e.g. "othermod:*" matches all dimensions added by "othermod"
ftbchunks.claim_dimension_whitelist.tool:
List of dimension ID's where chunks may be claimed. If non-empty, dimension *must* be in this list (and also not in "Dimension Blacklist").
Same syntax as for "Dimension Blacklist"
ftbchunks.no_wilderness.tooltip:
If true, chunks must be claimed before modifying.
Overrides "Protect Unclaimed Regions Per-Dimension" when true
ftbchunks.no_wilderness_dimensions.toolt:
List of dimension ID's where chunks must be claimed before modifying.
E.g. add "minecraft:the_nether" to require chunks to be claimed in the Nether.
Wildcards are allowed, e.g. "othermod:*" matches all dimensions added by "othermod"
ftbchunks.max_idle_days_before_unclaim.t:
If no team member logs in for this many days,
the team's claims will be released.
Setting this to 0 disables auto-unclaiming.
ftbchunks.max_idle_days_before_unforce.t:
If no team member logs in for this many days,
any force-loaded chunks will no longer be force-loaded.
Setting this to 0 disables auto-unforceloading.
ftbchunks.long_range_tracker_interval.to:
Interval in ticks to send updates to clients with long-range player tracking data.
Lower values mean more frequent updates but more server load and network traffic;
 be careful with this, especially on busy servers.
Setting this to 0 disables long-range tracking.
ftbchunks.protect_unknown_explosions.too:
Some explosion sources (e.g. Ghasts) can't be determined in code.
If this setting is true, damage from these explosion is prevented in protected chunks.
ftbchunks.hard_team_claim_limit.tooltip:
Hard claim limit for party teams, regardless of member count or Party Limit Calculation mode.
Default of 0 means no hard limit.
ftbchunks.hard_team_force_limit.tooltip:
Hard force-load limit for party teams, regardless of member count or Party Limit Calculation mode.
Default of 0 means no hard limit.
ftbchunks.party_limit_mode.tooltip:
Method by which party claim & force-load limits are calculated.
LARGEST: use the limits of the member with the largest limits
SUM: add up all the members' limits
OWNER: use the party owner's limits only
AVERAGE: use the average of all members' limits.
ftbchunks.require_game_stage.tooltip: If true, players must have the 'ftbchunks_mapping' game stage (KubeJS and/or Gamestages required) to be able to open the map or see the minimap
ftbchunks.location_mode_override.tooltip: If true, team "Location Visibility" settings are ignored, and all players can see each other anywhere on the map
ftbchunks.memory.region_release_time.too:
Timeout in seconds to release data for 512x512 regions which haven't been accessed recently
Smaller values mean less memory usage, but more disk access as released regions are reloaded
Set to 0 to disable releasing of region data.
ftbchunks.memory.autorelease_on_map_clos:
When the large map is closed, auto-release region data down to this number.
Smaller values mean less memory usage, but more disk access as released regions are reloaded
Set to 0 to disable releasing of region data.
ftbchunks.memory.max_zoom_constraint.too:
When true, max map zoom-out is limited by the number of explored regions and amount of available memory.
If this is bothersome, set this to false.
advancements.bygonenether.acquire_wither: Acquire the Wither Waltz Music Disc
advancements.bygonenether.catacomb.title: Wither Or Not...
advancements.bygonenether.citadel.title: The Citadel in the Midgame
advancements.bygonenether.root.title: Bygone Nether
advancements.bygonenether.root.descripti: Explore the Nether for New Structures!
advancements.bygonenether.summon_enderma: Trim the Warp off of an Enderman
power.arkwys.credits.description: Origins made by Arkwys and Aiko_Suzuki
origin.arkwys.demon.name: Demon
origin.arkwys.demon.description: Creatures of the night, weakened when exposed to the sun but stronger in the shadows, demons travel the lands while eating souls to become stronger.
power.arkwys.demon/blood_drinker.name: Blood Drinker
power.arkwys.demon/blood_drinker.descrip: You must kill to recover hunger and saturation. The 'brown' bar with the 'steak' logo appears when the cooldown is active between the times you can kill to eat.
power.arkwys.demon/blood_sacrifice.name: Blood Sacrifice
power.arkwys.demon/blood_sacrifice.descr: Once you have eaten 100 souls, you unlock your [Secondary Ability]. The Ability to make a blood sacrifice which gives you Strength I and Resistance I. The 'orange' bar with the 'wither skeleton' shows cooldown of ability.
power.arkwys.demon/cursed_armor.name: Cursed Body
power.arkwys.demon/cursed_armor.descript: You can only wear armor with Curse enchantment or armor with values equal or lower to Iron Gear.
power.arkwys.demon/dash.name: Dash
power.arkwys.demon/dash.description: Your [Primary Ability] is a dash towards the direction you are looking at. The ability has 4 charges that restores over time.
power.arkwys.demon/more_energy.name: High Stamina
power.arkwys.demon/more_energy.descripti: You don't exhaust as fast as other races.
power.arkwys.demon/night_vision.name: Nocturnal
power.arkwys.demon/night_vision.descript: Being a creature of the night, you can see perfectly fine in the dark.
power.arkwys.demon/soul_eater.name: Soul Eater
power.arkwys.demon/soul_eater.descriptio: The 'red' bar with the 'blood' symbol shows how many souls you have. Each time you die you lose 50 souls. Less than 300 gives you regeneration I and speed I, Less than 600 gives you regeneration II and speed I and at 600 you have regeneration II and speed II.
power.arkwys.demon/sun.name: Extreme Heliophobia
power.arkwys.demon/sun.description: As a demon, you'll weaken (Mining Fatigue and Hunger), on top of that, any form of healing will be disabled from being exposed to sun.
origin.arkwys.slimefolk.name: Slimefolk
origin.arkwys.slimefolk.description: Being a slimefolk you are made of green slime, stronger in their natural habitat the swamp.
power.arkwys.slimefolk/high_jump.name: High Jump
power.arkwys.slimefolk/high_jump.descrip: Being a slime gives you the ability to jump higher (2 blocks).
power.arkwys.slimefolk/slime_health.name: Lower Health
power.arkwys.slimefolk/slime_size.name: Slime-sized
power.arkwys.slimefolk/slime_size.descri: You are really small compared to most creatures. (One Block Height)
power.arkwys.slimefolk/swamp_habitat.des: You were born in the swamp and staying there makes you feel better.
Your body is made of green slime. (Cosmetic)
origin.arkwys.woodelf.name: Wood Elf
origin.arkwys.woodelf.description: Inhabitant of the forests, elves are skillful in archery but weak in melee.
power.arkwys.woodelf/adept_projectiles.d: Elves deal significantly more damage using any type of projectile than other races.
power.arkwys.woodelf/forest_habitat.name: Forest Native
power.arkwys.woodelf/forest_habitat.desc: You were born in the land of bark and leaves and staying there makes you feel better.
power.arkwys.woodelf/last_stand.name: Last Stand
power.arkwys.woodelf/last_stand.descript: When low HP, you feel the urge to keep your ground. You gain resistance.
power.arkwys.woodelf/light_armoured.name: Light Armour User
power.arkwys.woodelf/light_armoured.desc: Owing to their slender nature, the heaviest armour elves can wear is netherite. (Only matters if you play with mods that add armours stronger then netherite.)
power.arkwys.woodelf/tall.name: Tall
power.arkwys.woodelf/tall.description: Elves are taller than 2 blocks (human height).
power.arkwys.woodelf/vegetarian.name: Vegetarian
power.arkwys.woodelf/vegetarian.descript: Elves put animal lives at the same value as any intelligent race, they do not eat any meat.
power.arkwys.woodelf/weak_melee.name: Physically Weaker
power.arkwys.woodelf/weak_melee.descript: Elves aren't strong in close combat using swords or axes. They do less damage with those weapon types.
origin.arkwys.piglinbrute.name: Piglin Brute
origin.arkwys.piglinbrute.description: Stronger variant of piglins that uses brute force to get what it wants.
power.arkwys.brute/all_that_glitters.des: Golden tools deal extra damage and golden armor has additional protection. Golden equipment lasts much longer, but non golden and non netherite equipment breaks faster. Armor made of netherite gives small speed boost.
power.arkwys.brute/axe_efficient.name: Axe Wielder
power.arkwys.brute/axe_efficient.descrip: Gold axes and netherite axes deal more damage, as brutes are efficient with them.
power.arkwys.brute/bastion_spawn.name: Bastion Spawn
power.arkwys.brute/bastion_spawn.descrip: As a piglin brute, your spawn is within a Bastion Remnant
power.arkwys.brute/soul_spooked.name: Soul Spooked
power.arkwys.brute/soul_spooked.descript: You are afraid of Soul Fire, becoming weak when near it.
origin.arkwys.deer.name: Deer
origin.arkwys.deer.description: Inhabitant of the forests and galloper of the wild, they are serene beasts that are quite mobile.
power.arkwys.deer/forest_native.name: Forest Native
power.arkwys.deer/forest_native.descript: You were born in the land of bark and leaves and staying there makes you feel better.
power.arkwys.deer/forrest_gump.name: Forrest Gump
power.arkwys.deer/forrest_gump.descripti: You feel the swift breeze through the green life of the wooden inhabited land. It makes you faster.
power.arkwys.deer/jump_bonus.name: High Jump
power.arkwys.deer/oh_deer_god.name: OH DEER GOD
power.arkwys.deer/oh_deer_god.descriptio: When low HP, you feel the urge to escape. You gain speed and weakness
power.arkwys.deer/sensitive_awareness.de: By pressing your [Primary Ability] key, you detect players in a 50 block radius. (If a player is in a 50 block radius a sound is made.)
power.arkwys.deer/weak.name: Weak
origin.arkwys.minotaur.name: Minotaur
origin.arkwys.minotaur.description: Monster of the labyrinth, the minotaur has decided to embark in a journey of it's own.
power.arkwys.minotaur/agoraphobia.name: Agoraphobia
power.arkwys.minotaur/agoraphobia.descri: Your eternal lifetime in the labyrinth has made you scared of the outside world. Spending too much time in open spaces weaken you, but being in closed areas make you more powerful
power.arkwys.minotaur/armor.name: Minotaur Physiology
power.arkwys.minotaur/armor.description: Your minotaur legs offer no possibility of wearing normal leggings and boots.
power.arkwys.minotaur/axe_proficiency.de: Axes are your weapon of choice. You deal +4 Damage with Axes.
power.arkwys.minotaur/big.name: Minotaur Shape
power.arkwys.minotaur/big.description: You are slightly bigger than the typical human.
power.arkwys.minotaur/fire.name: Not so fond of fire
power.arkwys.minotaur/fire.description: Your body hair tends to not like incoming fire. (More damage from fire)
power.arkwys.minotaur/health.name: Tough
power.arkwys.minotaur/health.description: Your time spent in the labyrinth made you more resilient.
power.arkwys.minotaur/hungry.name: Hungry
power.arkwys.minotaur/hungry.description: You need to eat more to use your abilities.
power.arkwys.minotaur/milk_tag.name: Milk-able Minotaur
power.arkwys.minotaur/milk_tag.descripti: You can milk yourself every day or so. That mystical milk can regenerate anyone that drinks it.
power.arkwys.minotaur/no_swim.name: Sturdy
power.arkwys.minotaur/no_swim.descriptio: Your legs weren't made for swimming. Because of that, you can't swim.
power.arkwys.minotaur/ram.name: Ram
power.arkwys.minotaur/ram.description: You can ram into your enemies to do considerable damage and get yourself closer to your enemy
origin.arkwys.moth.name: Moth
origin.arkwys.moth.description: Moths are sneaky bugs with an odd appetite for natural fibers and an infatuation with lamps and lights.
power.arkwys.moth/affinity.name: Light Affinity
power.arkwys.moth/affinity.description: Due to your infatuation with light, you gain various buffs around different light sources.
power.arkwys.moth/climbing.name: Four-Armed
power.arkwys.moth/climbing.description: Your race was born with four arms. This allows you to climb vertical surfaces. Use [Secondary Ability] to toggle on or off.
power.arkwys.moth/daytime.name: Overwhelming Light
power.arkwys.moth/daytime.description: Your eyes are only used to darkness and low light, the sun is too much for you to comprehend. You feel overwhelmed in its presence.
power.arkwys.moth/elytra_flight.name: Wings
power.arkwys.moth/elytra_flight.descript: As a moth you have wings! You can fly using elytra.
Due to your moth ancestors you have quite the taste for natural fibers. You are able to eat wool and leather among other things. Use [Primary Ability] while holding the item.
power.arkwys.moth/fire.name: Flammable Body
power.arkwys.moth/fire.description: Your body and wings are lightweight and cannot withstand scorching, you take double damage from fire sources.
power.arkwys.moth/fragile.name: Lightweight
power.arkwys.moth/fragile.description: Your body is lighter than others. You have 9 hearts.
power.arkwys.moth/night_vision.name: Compound Vision
power.arkwys.moth/night_vision.descripti: Your big moth eyes have adapted to see within dark spaces.
power.arkwys.moth/nimble.name: Nimble
power.arkwys.moth/nimble.description: Being a moth has its own perks, you are naturally lighter. You are immune to fall damage and velocity based damage.
power.arkwys.moth/water_slowness.name: Hydrophobic
power.arkwys.moth/water_slowness.descrip: Your wings and body are very fluffy, water slows you down.
origin.medievalorigins.arachnae.name: Arachnae
origin.medievalorigins.arachnae.descript: Humanoid, arachnid half-breeds, Arachnae are the size of a man with the dexterity and nimbleness of a spider. What could possibly go wrong?
origin.medievalorigins.banshee.name: Banshee
origin.medievalorigins.banshee.descripti: Banshees are spirits whose cries can shatter glass and drive people to suicide. They are also seen as an omen of death in mythology.
origin.medievalorigins.daemon.name: Daemon
origin.medievalorigins.daemon.descriptio: Daemons are evil, servants of Satan. This gives them numerous advantages, but it can also be their downfall.
origin.medievalorigins.dwarf.name: Dwarf
origin.medievalorigins.dwarf.description: Dwarves are short humanoids who live underground. They excel in mining, but have issues surviving above ground.
origin.medievalorigins.elf.name: Elf
origin.medievalorigins.elf.description: Elves are intelligent, long-living residents of the forest. Their skills in archery prove useful from afar, but their frailness becomes an issue up close.
origin.medievalorigins.fae.name: Fae
origin.medievalorigins.fae.description: Beings of magic, fae are capable of far more than regular humans. Whether that is a blessing or a curse; that is for you to decide...
origin.medievalorigins.goblin.name: Goblin
origin.medievalorigins.goblin.descriptio: Conniving and greedy, goblins excel in one-on-one combat and gain more loot from any mobs that they kill, although their small size becomes an issue against groups of foes.
origin.medievalorigins.gorgon.name: Gorgon
origin.medievalorigins.gorgon.descriptio: Gorgons turn their enemies to stone. However, life without being able to look anyone in the eye comes with consequences...
origin.medievalorigins.knight.name: Knight
origin.medievalorigins.knight.descriptio: Knights are valorous heroes, who work tirelessly to protect the land.
origin.medievalorigins.necromancer.name: Necromancer
origin.medievalorigins.necromancer.descr: Mages learnt in the art of raising the dead, Necromancers can raise an army from nothing. However, this morbid relationship with death comes with consequences...
origin.medievalorigins.ogre.name: Ogre
origin.medievalorigins.ogre.description: Large and impervious brutes, ogres are ferocious creatures with a grand stature. However, their appetite is insatiable, and their stature is just as often a hindrance as it is a help.
origin.medievalorigins.paladin.name: Paladin
origin.medievalorigins.paladin.descripti: Soldiers of the lord, Paladins excel in combat against the world's foul, undead creatures. However, their holiness leaves them vulnerable to attack from these very same beings...
origin.medievalorigins.pixie.name: Pixie
origin.medievalorigins.pixie.description: Agents of mischief, or harbingers of good fortune? Who ever said you can't be both!
origin.medievalorigins.plague_victim.des: Carrier of the Plague, it affects the victim's daily life yet does not kill them. Used correctly, it can be a powerful weapon against their foes.
origin.medievalorigins.siren.name: Siren
origin.medievalorigins.siren.description: Sirens have an ensnaring beauty and an evil nature, their irresistible beauty being the downfall of many a sailor. Its up to you to use this power to its full advantage.
origin.medievalorigins.troll.name: Troll
origin.medievalorigins.troll.description: Large, lumbering beasts of the mountains, trolls are by far the biggest and baddest brutes of the land. Yet, could this very size be their undoing?
origin.medievalorigins.werewolf.name: Werewolf
origin.medievalorigins.werewolf.descript: Ferocious animals, or people with a misunderstood condition? A werewolf can be either, which path will you choose?
origin.medievalorigins.yeti.name: Yeti
origin.medievalorigins.yeti.description: Lumbering giants of frosty peaks, the Yeti's icy nature allows them to stop almost any foe, but can leave them vulnerable to fiery attacks.
power.medievalorigins.arachnae/bottomles: A human sized spider does not come without consequences. A massive amount of food is required to sustain the Arachnae.
power.medievalorigins.arachnae/brittle.d: The Arachnae's exoskeleton cannot support armor heavier than iron.
power.medievalorigins.arachnae/climber.d: The fine bristles on the Arachnae's legs allow them to climb up walls.
power.medievalorigins.arachnae/fragile_e: The Arachnae's exoskeleton is vulnerable to damage. Their health is less compared to a regular human's.
power.medievalorigins.arachnae/many_eyes: The Arachnae's eight eyes are all adapted to darkness, and allow them to see clearly even with very little light.
power.medievalorigins.arachnae/venomous_: Arachnae's fangs contain venom, and every bite is a chance to poison their opponent.
power.medievalorigins.arachnae/web_sling: Arachnae can, on command, spin webs in which their opponents will be immobilized for a short while.
power.medievalorigins.banshee/ethereal.d: Banshees possess the ability to become intangible at will, meaning they cannot be affected by foes in the physical realm. This of course comes with a cooldown. Activated with the secondary power key.
power.medievalorigins.banshee/flesheater: Banshees feast upon the organs of the living. Their ethereal bodies have no desire for fruit or vegetables.
power.medievalorigins.banshee/hexed.name: Hexed
power.medievalorigins.banshee/hexed.desc: Banshees are known for their cursing prowess. Every time they are hit, there is a small chance that the attacker will be consigned to a fate of slow, agonizing death.
power.medievalorigins.banshee/immaterial: Being incorporeal does not come without consequence. Banshees have half the health a living person would have.
power.medievalorigins.banshee/iron_avers: Iron is lethal to banshees. They cannot bear to wear it.
power.medievalorigins.banshee/sonic_shri: Banshees are renowned for their supersonic cries, which can cause blood vessels to burst. Press [Primary Ability] and for a short period you will find yourself dealing far more damage.
power.medievalorigins.daemon/carnivore.d: A daemon's thirst for blood is insatiable. If it isn't the flesh of an animal, its worthless.
Imbued with Satan's power, the daemon can release a burst of hell's energy on command. Triggered with secondary power key.
power.medievalorigins.daemon/hellborne.d: When you've lived in the depths of hell, a lick of fire is nothing to you. Daemons are immune to fire damage.
When you've lived in lava your whole life, water seems quite scalding. Daemons are damaged by being in water.
power.medievalorigins.daemon/impure.name: Impure
power.medievalorigins.daemon/impure.desc: Daemons do not receive the positive effects from potions such as regeneration or instant health.
power.medievalorigins.daemon/overworld_w: As an agent of hell, daemons are not accustomed to the mobs of the overworld and take more damage from them.
power.medievalorigins.daemon/unholy_deal: Daemons can exchange some of their health for increased strength, on account of the devil's influence. Triggered by pressing G.
power.medievalorigins.dwarf/darkness_dwe: Dwarves are adapted for darkness. Daylight is far too strong for their eyes, and blinds them until darkness returns. Counteracted by wearing a golden helmet.
power.medievalorigins.dwarf/dense.name: Dense
power.medievalorigins.dwarf/dense.descri: Dwarves are heavy creatures for their size, and as a result cannot swim.
power.medievalorigins.dwarf/haste.name: Dwarf Technology
power.medievalorigins.dwarf/haste.descri: Dwarf Technology allows dwarves to mine significantly faster than other creatures.
power.medievalorigins.dwarf/miniature.de: Perhaps the most notable aspect of a dwarf is their size. They are far, far shorter than the average human.
power.medievalorigins.dwarf/nocturnal.de: Living underground has lead to dwarves having highly sensitive eyes, able to see perfectly fine even in the pitch black of the caverns.
power.medievalorigins.dwarf/photoallergi: Dwarf skin is not suited to the intense sunlight of the outside world, and they combust when exposed to it. Can be prevented by wearing a helmet.
Dwarves are known for their alcohol consumption. Press [Primary Ability] to consume a potent brew which brings health back to full.
power.medievalorigins.elf/archer.name: Archer
power.medievalorigins.elf/archer.descrip: Elves are expert marksmen. They deal significantly more damage using a bow than other creatures.
Centuries of living in the forest has given the elves far better perception in the dark than most.
power.medievalorigins.elf/hyper_sight.de: Elves' enhanced perception allows them to keep track of an enemy for a while after hitting them, even when they aren't in view.
power.medievalorigins.elf/spindly.name: Spindly
power.medievalorigins.elf/spindly.descri: Owing to their slender nature, the heaviest armor elves can wear is chain mail.
power.medievalorigins.elf/vegetarian.des: Elves live off of the forest and its fruits. Their digestive systems cannot process meat.
power.medievalorigins.elf/towering.name: Towering
power.medievalorigins.elf/towering.descr: Elves are substantially taller than the average human. Despite this, they are just as skinny...
power.medievalorigins.elf/weak_melee.des: Elves are built for combat from afar, not up close. Their damage with swords and axes is reduced.
power.medievalorigins.fae/allure.name: Allure
power.medievalorigins.fae/allure.descrip: Fae are naturally alluring. Unfortunately, this means that mobs will pursue them from far further away than they would other creatures.
power.medievalorigins.fae/diminutive.des: It is rare for a fae to break 5 feet in height. They are small creatures, even smaller than the weaselly goblins.
power.medievalorigins.fae/frail.name: Frail
power.medievalorigins.fae/frail.descript: Being small has its drawbacks. Fae' max health is reduced, as their small size makes them prone to damage.
Iron inhibits fae powers. It is unbearable for them to wear it.
power.medievalorigins.fae/levitation.des: Fae are known for their ability to levitate. Press [Primary Ability] and you will begin to hover.
power.medievalorigins.fae/magic_strength: As magical creatures themselves, fae take less magic damage compared to other creatures.
power.medievalorigins.fae/plant_immunity: You negate all damage coming from plants.
power.medievalorigins.fae/regen.name: Regeneration
power.medievalorigins.fae/regen.descript: Fae are magic creatures. Press your secondary power key and you will regenerate health for a short period, at the cost of your hunger.
power.medievalorigins.goblin/cunning.des: Goblins are cunning creatures. Their attacks do more damage than other creatures and they gain more loot from killing mobs.
power.medievalorigins.goblin/frail.name: Frail
power.medievalorigins.goblin/frail.descr: Being small has its drawbacks. Goblins' max health is reduced, as their small size makes them prone to damage.
power.medievalorigins.goblin/greedy.name: Greedy
power.medievalorigins.goblin/greedy.desc: Goblins have a naturally greedy disposition. Anything gilded gives significantly more benefit to them than it would to others.
power.medievalorigins.goblin/nippy.name: Nippy
power.medievalorigins.goblin/nippy.descr: Although short, goblins are most certainly not slow. Moderate increase to base movement speed.
power.medievalorigins.goblin/stunted.des: Goblins' poor diets and genetics prevent them from growing as tall as other creatures.
power.medievalorigins.gorgon/hydrophobe_: Gorgons take damage from water, as they are fundamentally evil creatures who cannot stand the purity of water.
power.medievalorigins.gorgon/petrificati: The gorgons were cursed with being bound in dark, dank caves. Being outside in daylight causes them to become petrified until night. Can be negated by wearing a helmet.
power.medievalorigins.gorgon/serpentine_: Every time a gorgon is hit, they have a chance to spawn a silverfish to attack for them.
power.medievalorigins.gorgon/silver_aver: A gorgon's only real weakness is silver (Iron acts as silver). They cannot wear silver armour.
When a mob attacks a gorgon there is a chance for it to be frozen in place for a short period of time.
power.medievalorigins.gorgon/super_stren: Gorgons are renowned for their supernatural strength. They deal far more base damage than any other creature.
power.medievalorigins.knight/burdened.de: Burdened by heavy armor, knights have reduced movement speed.
power.medievalorigins.knight/for_honour_: What's a knight without his shining armor? Iron armor provides significantly more defense than it does to others.
power.medievalorigins.knight/magic_prone: With high physical damage resistance, it is only natural that attacks of a more spectral nature have increased effects on knights.
Unskilled in the art of archery, knights are incapable of using bows.
power.medievalorigins.knight/skilled_swo: Knights are trained professionals at what they do. Any attack they make with a sword deals more damage.
power.medievalorigins.knight/valour.name: Valor
power.medievalorigins.knight/valour.desc: Knights are valorous men. In their dying moments, they fight harder than ever.
power.medievalorigins.necromancer/black_: Necromancers only work with death. They cannot harvest any crops, they wilt at their deathly touch.
power.medievalorigins.necromancer/distur: Learning the art of necromancy is traumatizing. Necromancers cannot sleep, too scared to dream of what they wish they did not know.
power.medievalorigins.necromancer/hellra: At will, a necromancer can raise a circle of skeletons, blocking projectiles and damaging other opponents. Unfortunately, it only lasts for a short time.
power.medievalorigins.necromancer/imperv: The study of death has made Necromancers immune to poison, wither and instant damage. Unfortunately, this also means they do not receive the positive effects from regeneration and instant health.
power.medievalorigins.necromancer/poor_r: Unfortunately, students of the dark arts are feared by the general populace. Villagers will refuse to trade with Necromancers and iron golems will attack them on sight. This does, however, come with the bonus that they are accepted amongst the ranks of the Pillagers.
power.medievalorigins.necromancer/resili: Learning about death goes a long way towards avoiding it. Necromancers have increased health.
power.medievalorigins.necromancer/risk_o: Every contact with a plague victim is a 50/50 on whether you will contract the disease or not. Their opponents best pray that they get lucky...
power.medievalorigins.necromancer/unguar: Enveloping oneself in the arcane leaves you open to attack in the physical realm. Most mobs deal more damage to necromancers.
power.medievalorigins.ogre/charge.name: Charge
power.medievalorigins.ogre/charge.descri: Ogres can charge forward, piercing through several blocks, but this drains hunger and slows the ogre for a short while.
power.medievalorigins.ogre/gargantuan.de: Ogres are renowned for their size, and are substantially taller (and wider) than most creatures.
power.medievalorigins.ogre/lead_belly.de: The enormous appetite of an ogre sometimes means eating an undesirable meal from time to time. As such, the ogre's stomach has evolved to withstand even the most toxic of foodstuffs.
power.medievalorigins.ogre/ravenous.name: Ravenous
power.medievalorigins.ogre/ravenous.desc: It takes a lot of food to sustain a creature as large as an ogre. Appetite is massively increased.
power.medievalorigins.ogre/sluggish.name: Sluggish
power.medievalorigins.ogre/sluggish.desc: Not known for their agility, ogres are some of the slowest creatures to roam the land.
power.medievalorigins.ogre/stocky.name: Stocky
power.medievalorigins.ogre/stocky.descri: Owing to their tremendous size, ogres have 2.5x the health of a regular player.
power.medievalorigins.ogre/xxxl.name: XXXL
power.medievalorigins.ogre/xxxl.descript: It is rather hard to find a suit of armor in size XXXL. As a result, ogres can only wear flexible armor, being leather and chain mail.
power.medievalorigins.paladin/holy_curse: As a servant of the Lord, paladins cannot bear to be in contact with impure beings such as undead mobs, and take more damage from them.
As a servant of the Lord, undead creatures cannot bear the touch of a paladin, and combust when hit.
power.medievalorigins.paladin/holy_instr: An axe in the hands of a Paladin is a dangerous weapon. All axes deal increased damage, but swords deal less damage.
power.medievalorigins.paladin/leech.name: Leech
power.medievalorigins.paladin/leech.desc: Every kill regenerates a heart of a Paladin's health.
power.medievalorigins.paladin/ravenous_w: Walking around in heavy armor all day is a chore. Paladins need more food to sustain themselves.
power.medievalorigins.paladin/weak_sword: A sword in the hands of a Paladin is a less powerful weapon.
power.medievalorigins.pixie/curse_of_fli: The wings which allows pixies to fly also prevent even the most skilled of craftsmen from creating a chest plate to accommodate them.
power.medievalorigins.pixie/feather_foot: The pixie's small size means it is completely impossible for them to take fall damage.
power.medievalorigins.pixie/flight.name: Flight
power.medievalorigins.pixie/flight.descr: Pixies are blessed with the gift of flight.
power.medievalorigins.pixie/good_fortune: Although pixies can be troublesome, they are also associated with good luck. When mining, you will occasionally get something valuable from plain stone.
power.medievalorigins.pixie/mischief_mak: Pixies are capable of performing numerous mischievous acts which, if not not dangerous, are certainly loud.
power.medievalorigins.pixie/pixie_proper: Pixies are some of the smallest creatures to roam the land, rarely reaching even the height of a regular person's knee.
power.medievalorigins.pixie/soaked.name: Soaked
power.medievalorigins.pixie/soaked.descr: Being as small as they are, water poses significant threat to pixies. It hampers their movement and impairs their ability to fly.
power.medievalorigins.pixie/troublemaker: Villagers know pixies by the legends of trouble they cause, and will refuse to trade with them.
power.medievalorigins.plague_victim/cont: The Plague is highly contagious. Villagers will refuse to trade with you out of fear of contracting the plague.
power.medievalorigins.plague_victim/foul: Plague carrying fleas swarm the victim. Being in the general vicinity of them is not beneficial for one's health.
power.medievalorigins.plague_victim/inso: The horrible welts make sleep impossible for carriers of the Plague to sleep.
power.medievalorigins.plague_victim/plag: Although the plague affects the carrier, they do not suffer the brunt of its symptoms. Carriers are immune to poison and wither.
power.medievalorigins.plague_victim/risk: Every contact with a plague victim is a 50/50 on whether you will contract the disease or not. Their opponents best pray that they get lucky...
power.medievalorigins.plague_victim/sens: The Plague causes welts and lesions upon the skin, which are tender and painful to touch. As a result, victims cannot wear armor for the pain it causes.
power.medievalorigins.plague_victim/skin: The Plague causes rapid muscle atrophy, resulting in reduced health and speed.
power.medievalorigins.siren/amphibious.d: Sirens, being a subset of merpeople, can survive in water, and swim with increased speed.
power.medievalorigins.siren/flammable.de: Sirens and fire do not mix well. Any contact with flames results in instant death. Be sure to watch your step in the nether!
power.medievalorigins.siren/holy_water.d: Sirens have regenerative powers, which are at full force when they are in water.
power.medievalorigins.siren/out_of_your_: Although sirens can survive just fine on land, it is not their natural environment. As such, their regenerative abilities do not apply, and any damage taken can only be healed with potions.
power.medievalorigins.siren/prone.name: Prone
power.medievalorigins.siren/prone.descri: While sirens can regenerate their bodies, they are weak to blunt force. Melee attacks do more damage to them.
power.medievalorigins.siren/siren_song.d: Sirens are known for their alluring calls. Press [Primary capacity] to make all mobs around you neutral until hit. (DOES NOT APPLY TO BOSSES, FOR OBVIOUS REASONS)
power.medievalorigins.siren/water_vision: Sirens have superior underwater vision than other creatures.
power.medievalorigins.troll/apex_predato: Trolls cannot eat regular foodstuffs, and can only satiate their hunger by slaughtering other creatures.
power.medievalorigins.troll/ham_fisted.d: While the huge fists of the troll pack a mighty punch, they are far too cumbersome to hold a shield.
power.medievalorigins.troll/ironhide.des: Trolls have incredibly thick skin, giving them a natural armor and massively increased health.
power.medievalorigins.troll/lumbering.de: When you're as large as a troll, you have a lot of weight to heft around. Movement is noticeably slower than one would expect for their size.
Trolls take after the mountains from which they come from. They are massively tall, twice the size of the average person.
power.medievalorigins.troll/old_blood.de: The old blood which runs through the veins of the trolls is bound to the mountains. They cannot heal themselves outside of their hilly homelands.
power.medievalorigins.troll/out_of_stock: Try as they might, trolls never seem to be able to find any armor in their size. Thus, they are doomed to walk with what coverings nature gave them, and nothing more.
power.medievalorigins.troll/rock_throw.d: A troll can, at will, hurl a large rock into the air, plowing through whatever may cross its path. However, this does come at the cost of 64 precious cobblestone blocks.
power.medievalorigins.troll/thunderous_s: Trolls walk with purpose. Should they persist long enough, they can walk straight through any obstacle which may cross their path.
power.medievalorigins.werewolf/carnivore: Werewolves eat like a wolf, even when not transformed. The only food they can eat is meat.
power.medievalorigins.werewolf/drained.d: Increased prowess at night does, unfortunately, come with consequences. In daytime your health and strength are reduced.
power.medievalorigins.werewolf/insatiabl: Werewolves are constantly looking for their next meal. Their appetite is much greater than average.
power.medievalorigins.werewolf/lycanthro: The condition which causes werewolves to turn into a wolf at night. Has the effect of increasing a person's stature, strength and health.
power.medievalorigins.werewolf/silver_av: Werwolves are very weak to silver. They cannot bear to wear it. (Iron acts as silver)
power.medievalorigins.yeti/flammable.des: Yetis are susceptible to fire damage due to their wintry nature.
A powerful magic runs through the veins of a yeti, allowing them to entomb a group of foes in ice on command.
power.medievalorigins.yeti/from_whence_y: Thriving best in the lands from which they originate, yetis move faster and are carried on the snow to negate fall damage in icy biomes.
power.medievalorigins.yeti/frosty_breath: The frosty breath of the yeti slows any opponents which get close to them.
power.medievalorigins.yeti/thick_fur.des: The blessing of thick fur becomes a curse in deserts. Your movement is slowed and health reduced to that of a normal person.
power.medievalorigins.yeti/titanic.name: Titanic
power.medievalorigins.yeti/titanic.descr: Yetis have far more health than a regular human.
power.medievalorigins.yeti/unstoppable.d: Yetis are immune to the slowness effect.
power.medievalorigins.yeti/winter_body.d: Yetis are marginally taller than a regular human, and significantly wider.
medievalorigins.contagious_villager: The villager doesn't want to be infected!
medievalorigins.disturbed_restless: What you know will kill you, but you will die laughing.
medievalorigins.insomniac_welts: Your welts sting and burn. There will be no sleep for you tonight.
medievalorigins.poor_reputation_villager: The villager is too scared to trade with you!
medievalorigins.troublemaker: Villagers don't trade with the likes of you!

biomepedia.biome.byg.allium_fields.desc: Lush flowering fields with Pink & Purple Allium Bushes. Large oak trees and villages can be commonly found here.
biomepedia.biome.byg.amaranth_fields.des: Lush flowering fields with Red, Magenta, Cyan, Orange, & Purple Amaranth Flower Bushes can be found here. Tropical jacaranda trees & jacaranda bushes.
biomepedia.biome.byg.araucaria_savanna.d: A dry yet floral savanna with canopy araucaria trees & acacia trees. Savanna villages can be commonly found here.
biomepedia.biome.byg.arisian_undergrowth: A Nether Biome that has been disabled until further reworks planned.
biomepedia.biome.byg.aspen_forest.desc: The Aspen Forest is home to lots of lush flora such as Pink Alliums, Rose, Yellow Daffodils, and Orange Daisies. Dense amounts of aspen trees can be found here along with Taiga Villages.
biomepedia.biome.byg.atacama_desert.desc: A vibrant and floral desert with an abundance of Barrel Cacti, Cacti, Golden Spined Cacti, Prickly Pear Cacti, Aloe Vera, Anemones, & Sages. In the real world, the Atacama Desert is located in Chile, South America along the Pacific Coast!
biomepedia.biome.byg.autumnal_forest.des: An Oak and Birch forest locked in a permanent Fall Season. White Puffballs can be found here along with Podzol and many flowers! It is rumored there have been sightings of Pumpkin Wards here and some players have even stumbled upon their Pumpkin Patch.
biomepedia.biome.byg.autumnal_taiga.desc: A Spruce and Aspen taiga locked in a permanent Fall Season. It is rumored there have been sightings of Pumpkin Wards here and some players have even stumbled upon their Pumpkin Patch. Players have also found Taiga Villages within this biome, I wonder if there is a connection?
biomepedia.biome.byg.autumnal_valley.des: An vibrant valley with Lush Grass Blocks & Lush Dirt, massive pumpkins can be found here with lots of Clovers and flowers! It is rumored there have been sightings of Pumpkin Wards here and some players have even stumbled upon their Pumpkin Patch.
biomepedia.biome.byg.baobab_savanna.desc: A dry savanna with bulky Baobab Trees and Acacia Trees. The fruit from the Baobab gives great satisfaction in times of desperation, players have also stumbled upon Savanna Villages here.
biomepedia.biome.byg.basalt_barrera.desc: A unique beach biome with Basalt Pillars and occasional surface Deepslate.
biomepedia.biome.byg.bayou.desc: An murky swamp filled with Willow Trees. Players can find Cattails, Mud, Clay, and lots of flowers! Witch Huts have been spotted here..
biomepedia.biome.byg.black_forest.desc: An eerie forest filled with Pine, Aspen and Coniferous trees. Players can find Black Roses here along with other flowers and Taiga Villages have been spotted here.
biomepedia.biome.byg.borealis_grove.desc: A cold temperature grove with reworks in its future!
biomepedia.biome.byg.brimstone_caverns.d: A toxic cavern filled with Brim Fire and Anthracite. Players can find Bastion Remnants & Nether Fortresses here as well.
biomepedia.biome.byg.bulbis_gardens.desc: An alien and strange garden with tangled Bulbis Oddities. Players can find End Cities and Bulbis Anomalies here.
biomepedia.biome.byg.canadian_shield.des: A highland region home to the beautiful Hydrangea Flower. Players can find Aspen, Spruce, Pine, & Confierous Trees here. Spruce Villages are common here along with Mossy Cobblestone.
biomepedia.biome.byg.cardinal_tundra.des: A desolate yet vibrant tundra. Players can find lots of Rabbits here and the occasional Snow Village.
biomepedia.biome.byg.cherry_blossom_fore: A blossoming Sakura Forest home to variety of Cherry Blossom trees with the occasional Birch tree. Players can find an abundance of animals, flowers, and decorational blocks here and it has a beautiful aesthetic.
biomepedia.biome.byg.cika_woods.desc: An ancient and mysterious autumnal taiga. Players can find large pumpkins, cika trees, and it is rumored there have been sightings of Pumpkin Wards here and some players have even stumbled upon their Pumpkin Patch.
biomepedia.biome.byg.coconino_meadow.des: A open vibrant highland meadow with shrubs, sunflowers, tulips, lots of vegetation and Lush Grass Blocks/Lush Dirt. Ancient Ruin Villages can be found here as well as Spruce Villages. In the real world, the Coconino Meadow is located in Arizona, USA in the Northern Region near the Grand Canyon.
biomepedia.biome.byg.coniferous_forest.d: A dense taiga with towering Confierous trees, occasional Spruce trees can also be found here. Mossy Boulders and lush cold vegetation/flora can be found here. Spruce Villages can also be seen commonly.
biomepedia.biome.byg.crag_gardens.desc: A magical tropical garden located in warm regions of the world. Players can find an abundance of tropical vegetation and Rainbow Eucalyptus trees.
biomepedia.biome.byg.crimson_gardens.des: A blissful garden deep within the Nether Caverns. Players can find Crimson Berry Bushes, Bastion Remnants, & Nether Fortresses here as well.
biomepedia.biome.byg.cryptic_wastes.desc: A desolate scorched area with Cryptic Fire and Cryptic Stone. Players can find unique Cryptic Vents throughout the biome as well as Therium Deposits.
A lush swampland with Cypress trees. Players can find swamp vegetation & flora here along with unique mobs like Frogs. Witch Huts have also been spotted in the area.
biomepedia.biome.byg.dacite_ridges.desc: A highland mountain biome with large Holly & Spruce trees. Players can find unique Dacite Stone and plenty of taiga vegetation.
biomepedia.biome.byg.dacite_shore.desc: A unique beach shoreline that contains Dacite Stone.
biomepedia.biome.byg.prairie.desc: A vibrant and hilly grassland with Prairie Grass & Tall Prairie Grass. California Poppies, large oak trees, and villages can be commonly found here.
biomepedia.biomeabout.dimensions.none: This biome doesn't spawn in any dimension.
biomepedia.biomeabout.mobspawns.none: This biome doesn't spawn any mobs.
biomepedia.desc.block.byg.pendorite_bloc:
This is a Pendorite Block, and if you managed to get this, you're genuinely flexing at this point.
Like how did you do it and how are you so cool like whoaaaaa.

Anyways if you made it this far, you're cool for reading this :)
biomepedia.intro:
Hi and welcome to the Oh The Biomes You'll Go(or "BYG" for short) biomepedia! Here you'll find information in regards to our biomes, blocks, items, tools, and more! On the right hand page, select the item you're looking for.

Thank you for playing BYG! <3
Learn more about BYG's blocks & items!

lore.aquamirae.frozen_key: Opens a chest hidden in the depths of the Ice Maze.
lore.aquamirae.golden_moth_in_a_jar: Some treasures can have their own souls, not only devour others...
lore.aquamirae.luminescent_bubble: Increases the swimming speed of nearby players. Place afloat to build underwater roads.
lore.aquamirae.pirate_pouch: {I}Press {U} to open. > Forgotten pirate clothes that smell like rotten oysters...
lore.aquamirae.poseidons_breakfast: Food of the Sea Gods. > Fury X (3:00) > Rush V (3:00) > > When Consumed: > +100% Ability Power > +50% Cooldown Reduction
lore.aquamirae.rune_of_the_storm: {I}Press {U} to use. > Attaches to the sword in your off hand, increasing its damage in cold biomes by 33%.
lore.aquamirae.sea_casserole: Is it looking at me? > Rush II (1:30) > Strength (0:30) > > When Consumed: > +20% Cooldown Reduction > +3 Attack Damage
lore.aquamirae.sea_stew: The power of the sea in your stomach! > Fury III (2:00) > Strength (2:00) > > When Consumed: > +30% Ability Power > +3 Attack Damage
lore.aquamirae.shell_horn: {B}Summons Captain Cornelia. > Can be used near water in an Ice Maze.
lore.aquamirae.ship_graveyard_echo: If you listen carefully, you can hear the horns of hundreds of ships lost in the Ice Maze...
lore.aquamirae.treasure_pouch: {I}Press {U} to open. > Once valuable loot, now worthless trinkets under the ice... May contain a Ship or Outpost map.
lore.aquamirae.wisteria_niveis: Even in the midst of an icy wasteland, a wonderful life can appear. Can be placed.

effect.alexsmobs.bug_pheromones.descript: Make hostile arthropods neutral to the user.
effect.alexsmobs.debilitating_sting.desc: An Effect which poisons the victim but paralyzes arthropods. It will stop if the victim is at half health and is not an arthropod. Inflicted by a Tarantula Hawk.
effect.alexsmobs.ender_flu.description: After the effect runs out naturally, the user takes massive damage and an Enderiophage will spawn. Inflicted by an Enderiophage.
effect.alexsmobs.fear.description: Makes the target unable to move. Effect applied when a Tiger reveals itself to the user.
effect.alexsmobs.oiled.description: Oil floats on water. Cover yourself in oil to float on the surface of water and outside in the rain.
effect.alexsmobs.orcas_might.description: Grants increased attack speed. Effect may be applied when swimming with an Orca.
effect.alexsmobs.soulsteal.description: Grants the user attacks some life-steal.
effect.alexsmobs.sunbird_blessing.descri: Decreases fall speed, prevents fall damage and makes it easier to fly with an Elytra or Tarantula Hawk Elytra. Effect is applied when near a Sunbird.
effect.alexsmobs.sunbird_curse.descripti: Increases fall speed, causing the user to hit the ground quicker. This effectively impedes the use of an Elytra. Effect is applied when attacking a Sunbird.
effect.alexsmobs.tigers_blessing.descrip: Tigers near the user will be neutral and will protect them from hostile foes. The effect will go away early when attacking a Tiger. Applied by feeding a Tiger chicken or pork chops.
effect.alexsmobs.fleet_footed.descriptio: Increases player speed whilst jumping and sprinting.
effect.alexsmobs.power_down.description: Hello, hello? Uhh, I wanted to record a message for you...
enchantment.alexsmobs.straddle_jump.desc: Increases the height of Straddleboard jumps.
enchantment.alexsmobs.lavawax.desc: Gives the rider of the Straddleboard Fire Resistance.
enchantment.alexsmobs.serpentfriend.desc: Makes Bone Serpents neutral towards the rider of the Straddleboard.
enchantment.alexsmobs.board_return.desc: Straddleboard returns instantly to the rider's inventory when broken.
