How long you need to hover an anchor area/element
to change the anchor point of an element.
fancymenu.editor.anchor_overlay.invert_c:
Inverts the colors of what's behind the overlay,
so the overlay is always visible.

Enabling this disables custom colors and opacity.
fancymenu.editor.auto_scaling.disable_fo:
You need to disable auto-scaling first
before editing the forced GUI scale.
fancymenu.editor.background.blur_backgro:
If Vanilla's background blur should get
applied to the custom background.
fancymenu.editor.background.show_overlay: Show Dark Overlay On Custom Background: %s

If the dark overlay rendered by Vanilla Minecraft
should be visible on custom backgrounds.
fancymenu.editor.background_options.copy:
This will copy the identifier of the
current menu background to the clipboard.

The background identifier is used by actions, placeholders
and similar stuff to communicate with the background instance.
fancymenu.editor.buddy.enable.desc:
If a cute little pet creature should
walk around at the bottom of the editor screen.
fancymenu.editor.close_audio.desc: Play an audio when closing the screen.
fancymenu.editor.layout.index.desc:
The layout index is useful when you have
multiple layouts active for the same screen.
If these layouts need to get loaded
in a specific order, use the layout index.
The bigger the index, the later the layout
gets loaded, which means it is ON TOP OF
layouts with a smaller index.

For example: A layout with index 1 will
be under a layout with index 2.
fancymenu.editor.object.movedown.desc:
Moves the element one layer down.

IMPORTANT:
Selected elements are always on top,
so you will not see the change
until you deselect the element.
fancymenu.editor.object.moveup.desc:
Moves the element one layer up.

IMPORTANT:
Selected elements are always on top,
so you will not see the change
until you deselect the element.
fancymenu.editor.open_audio.desc: Play an audio when opening the screen.
fancymenu.editor.render_custom_behind_va:
If all non-vanilla elements should
get rendered behind vanilla elements.

Since you can't change the order
of vanilla elements, this is the only
way to have some kind of control over it.
fancymenu.editor.rightclick.scale.invali: Scale values can't be smaller than 0!
fancymenu.editor.saving_failed.generic:
Unable to save layout!
An error happened while trying to save the layout!
fancymenu.editor.settings.enable_element:
If elements should show controls for tilting them.
You can also set their vertical/horizontal tilt in their right-click menu.
fancymenu.editor.settings.enable_rotatio:
If elements should show controls for rotating them.
You can also set their rotation in their right-click menu.
fancymenu.editor.text_editor.single_line:
The target needs a single-line text, which means all lines will
get merged into one line and all leading spaces of all lines
except the very first line will get removed in the actual
output text for the target.
fancymenu.editor.warning.unsaved:
Are you sure?

All unsaved changes for the current layout will get lost!
fancymenu.element.auto_sizing.desc:
Auto-sizing will try to adjust the element's size
based on the screen size, so it's never too big or
too small for the current screen size.

It is not recommended to use this when
auto-scaling is enabled in the layout.
fancymenu.element.base_opacity.desc: Should be a floating point value between 0.0 and 1.0.
fancymenu.element.elements.splash_text.d:
A splash text like the bouncing
text in the Title screen.
fancymenu.element.fading.error.negative_:
Fading speed needs to be a positive and
valid floating point value (bigger than 0.0).
fancymenu.element.fading.fade_out.desc:
Fade-Out will NOT fade-out elements before opening a new menu!
It is meant to be used when elements change
their visibility via loading requirements.
fancymenu.element.general.pick_element.d:
List will all elements at the position
of the mouse cursor when
you opened this context menu.

Useful for when you need to
select an element that's behind
another one.
fancymenu.element.rotation.advanced_mode:
Enabling this allows you to use placeholders in the element's
rotation degrees value, but it will also disable rotation grabbers.
fancymenu.element.rotation.degrees.desc:
Set the rotation angle in degrees for this element.
Positive values rotate clockwise.

This is the same as using the grabbers,
but more precise for full control.
fancymenu.element.sticky_anchor.desc:
In this mode, the element's position will get calculated
in a different way than normal.

This mode makes the element always keep the exact same distance
to its anchor, no matter the current size of the element.
This means the size of the element can dynamically change
without it moving away or getting closer to its anchor.
While this can be useful in some situations, there
are also cases where this behaviour is not optimal.

This has NO EFFECT when using another element as anchor!
fancymenu.element.sticky_anchor.desc.dis: You need to disable 'Stay on Screen' first to use this!
fancymenu.element.tilt.horizontal.advanc:
Enabling this allows you to use placeholders in the element's
horizontal tilt degrees value, but it will also disable tilt grabbers.
fancymenu.element.tilt.horizontal.degree:
Set the horizontal tilt angle in degrees for this element.
Positive values tilt the right side away from the viewer.
Range: -60 to 60 degrees.

This is the same as using the grabbers,
but more precise for full control.
fancymenu.element.tilt.vertical.advanced:
Enabling this allows you to use placeholders in the element's
vertical tilt degrees value, but it will also disable tilt grabbers.

Positive values tilt the top away from the viewer.
Range: -60 to 60 degrees.

This is the same as using the grabbers,
but more precise for full control.

should get calculated.

You can see how an element
is affected by its anchor point
when you resize the editor window.

of the parent element here.

Audio elements allow you to play
audio files in screens.
Supports multiple audios per element!
fancymenu.elements.audio.disable_vanilla:
Disabling Vanilla Music in Screens

You can disable the music that plays in screens
in FancyMenu's menu bar at the top of every screen,
when you're NOT in the editor.

To toggle it off, disable: 
Customization -> Settings -> Play Vanilla Music in Screens
fancymenu.elements.audio.manage_audios.r:

Do you really want to remove the selected audio track?

Track weights affect how likely each track is to be selected in shuffle mode.

fancymenu.elements.browser.desc: A browser where you can load a URL (website) in.
fancymenu.elements.browser.disabled_in_e: The browser is not interactive while in the editor!
fancymenu.elements.browser.hide_video_co:
If the controls of all videos should be hidden.
This will probably not work in some cases.
If the user should be able ot interact with the browser.
fancymenu.elements.browser.loop_videos.d:
If all videos should loop.
This will probably not work in some cases.

Set the base volume of media elements like audios and videos.
Should be a value between 0.0 (0%) and 1.0 (100%).
This will probably not work in some cases.
fancymenu.elements.browser.mute_media.de:
If all audios and videos should get muted on load.
This will probably not work in some cases.
fancymenu.elements.browser.url.desc: The URL the browser should load.
fancymenu.elements.button.active_state_c:
Control when/if the widget should be enabled (clickable)
or disabled (not clickable and greyed out).
fancymenu.elements.button.manage_actions:
Manage the actions this button
should execute when clicked.
fancymenu.elements.button.template_setti:
When you enable the template mode for a custom button, it will apply
some of its settings to all other buttons or sliders in the current screen.

When you set the template to share settings with sliders, the
settings for the button textures will change to slider texture settings.

Settings that get shared are:

- Button/Slider Textures
- Button Click Sounds
- Button/Slider Hover Sounds
- Button/Slider Position (if enabled)
- Button/Slider Size (if enabled)
- Button/Slider Opacity (if enabled)
- Button/Slider Visibility (if enabled)
- Button/Slider Label (if enabled)
fancymenu.elements.button.tooltip.desc:
Tooltip to display when the widget is getting hovered.
If you need more control over the tooltip's design, use a dedicated Tooltip element.
fancymenu.elements.buttons.buttonbackgro:
The highlighted background is used
when focusing the slider by using the
arrow/tab key navigation in screens.
fancymenu.elements.checkbox.background_t: The hover background texture. The default texture is 20x20 pixels.
The inactive background texture. The default texture is 20x20 pixels.
The normal background texture. The default texture is 20x20 pixels.
fancymenu.elements.checkbox.checkmark_te:
The texture displayed when the checkbox is checked.
Leave empty to use the default checkmark.

The default checkmark texture is 20x20 pixels.
fancymenu.elements.checkbox.desc:
A clickable checkbox that can execute actions when toggled.

Use the '$$value' placeholder in its actions and loading requirements
to get the current checkbox state (true/false).
fancymenu.elements.checkbox.manage_actio:
Actions will be executed when the checkbox is toggled.

You can use the '$$value' placeholder in actions
to get the current checkbox state (true/false).
fancymenu.elements.copyid.desc:
Copy the ID of this element, to use
it in loading requirements, etc.

Make sure the texture is a PNG RGBA image
and is not too large.
32x32 or 64x64 pixel should be enough.
fancymenu.elements.cursor.desc:
A custom cursor that gets show
instead of the default one.

It's possible that the cursor behaviour
varies between operating systems.
fancymenu.elements.cursor.editor_preview:
Shows the custom cursor in the editor
when hovering over the cursor element.

The hotspot of a cursor is the
pixel of the cursor texture where
clicks get registered.
For a normal arrow cursor, this
would be the tip of the arrow.

The X0 Y0 coordinate of a texture
is at its top-left corner.

The hotspot of a cursor is the
pixel of the cursor texture where
clicks get registered.

would be the tip of the arrow.

The X0 Y0 coordinate of a texture
is at its top-left corner.
fancymenu.elements.deprecated_warning.li: DEPRECATED ELEMENT! This element type gets removed in the future!
There should be a new version of this element type.
You should replace this element with the new version.
fancymenu.elements.dragger.desc:
The Dragger allows you to make parts of your layout dragable,
which means users can "grab" parts of layouts with
the mouse cursor and move them around.
fancymenu.elements.dragger.save_offset.d:
If the drag offset should be persistent
or reset every time the menu gets reopened.
fancymenu.elements.element.load_once_per:
Enabling this will make the element only load once per game session.
It stays active/visible until the user opens a new screen.
The 'game session' ends when restarting the game.
fancymenu.elements.element.stay_on_scree:
Will prevent the element from going
out of the visible screen area
when resizing the window or changing
the GUI scale.
You need to disable 'Sticky Anchor' first to use this!
fancymenu.elements.features.advanced_pos:
ONLY FOR ADVANCED USERS!

Allows you to manually set the
position of the element.

Advanced positions support placeholders,
so you can calculate positions
by using the Calculator placeholder,
get positions of other elements
and much more.

Many useful placeholders for element
positioning can be found
in the "GUI" and "Advanced"
placeholder categories.

You will not be able to resize or
drag and move the element while this
feature is in use.
fancymenu.elements.features.advanced_siz:
ONLY FOR ADVANCED USERS!

Allows you to manually set the
size of the element.

Advanced sizes support placeholders,
so you can calculate sizes
by using the Calculator placeholder,
get sizes of other elements
and much more.

Many useful placeholders for element
sizing can be found
in the "GUI" and "Advanced"
placeholder categories.

You will not be able to resize
the element on axes that got
overridden by an advanced size.
fancymenu.elements.image.desc:
A simple image.
Supports local and web sources.
fancymenu.elements.image.restart_animate: Restart Animated Textures When Opening Screen: %s
fancymenu.elements.in_editor_color.desc: Set a custom in-editor color to help with organization.
fancymenu.elements.in_editor_display_nam:
The in-editor display name helps with organization.
It is shown in the layers widget and when
you pick an element using the right-click menu.
fancymenu.elements.input_field.desc:
A text input field.

Can be used to set variable
values by user input.
fancymenu.elements.input_field.editor.se:
Set the type of this text field.

The type defines what characters
the user can use in the field.

For example:
If the field is
set to "Only Numbers", the
user will only be able to
type numbers into the field.

Link this text field to a variable.
Use the variable name.

The variable can be a new
or an existing variable.
fancymenu.elements.item.desc:
An item like a sword, apple or grass block.
For the extra bit of battle pass menu flair!
fancymenu.elements.item.key.desc:
The registry key of the item.
Used to identify the item you want to display.
fancymenu.elements.item.lore.desc:
Set the lore of the item.
This input supports multiline and you
can even use 'Minecraft Text Components'.
Use one component (JSON) per line.

To learn more about text components, check this:
https://docs.fancymenu.net/en/text-formatting
fancymenu.elements.item.name: Set Item Name
fancymenu.elements.item.nbt.desc:
This allows you to set custom NBT data to the item.
It is basically the part the /give command that follows
after the item name in curly brackets {}.

Full example command:
/give @a netherite_sword{display:{Name:'["",{"text":"Kinabra","italic":false}]'}}

Set this as value for NBT:
{display:{Name:'["",{"text":"Kinabra","italic":false}]'}}

There are lots of Give Command Generators available online,
so just ask Google about it and you will find something.
fancymenu.elements.multiselect.loading_r:
Override Loading Requirements?

The selected elements have different loading requirements!
All of their loading requirements will get overridden!

Continue?
fancymenu.elements.music_controller.desc:
Element to control Vanilla music that plays in menus.

This element can't control music that plays
in worlds while no screen is open.
It is only to control music while a screen is open.
fancymenu.elements.music_controller.play:
This type of music plays in menus when NO world is loaded,
like in the Title screen for example.

This type of music plays in menus when a world is loaded.
It's basically the normal world music that
keeps playing in menus that don't pause the game,
like the inventory in SP and every menu in MP.
fancymenu.elements.parallax.desc:
If a parallax effect should get added to the element's position.

The parallax effect only works while not in the editor!
fancymenu.elements.parallax.intensity.de:
The intensity of the parallax effect.
This should be a value between 0.0 (no movement) and 1.0 (maximum movement).
fancymenu.elements.parallax.intensity.in: This needs to be a value between 0.0 (no movement) and 1.0 (maximum movement)!
fancymenu.elements.parallax.invert.desc:
When ENABLED, the element will move WITH the mouse.
When disabled, it will move in the opposite direction of the mouse.
fancymenu.elements.player_entity.baby.de: If the player should be a baby.
fancymenu.elements.player_entity.body_mo: If the player's pose should be animated.
fancymenu.elements.player_entity.cape.au:
You can't do this while
"Auto Cape" is enabled.

Tries to automatically pick
the cape based on the
element's player name.
fancymenu.elements.player_entity.copy_cl:
You can't do this while
"Copy Client Player" is enabled.

Automatically make the entity look
like the client player.

Copies the name, skin and cape.
If the player should have a parrot
on their shoulder.
fancymenu.elements.player_entity.parrot_:
If the player's shoulder parrot
should be on the left shoulder.
fancymenu.elements.player_entity.scale.d:
Set the entity's scale.

Default scale is 30.
fancymenu.elements.player_entity.set_pla:
Set the player's name.

You can use any name here,
it doesn't have to be an
existing user.
fancymenu.elements.player_entity.show_na: If the player name should be visible.
fancymenu.elements.player_entity.skin.au:
You can't do this while
"Auto Skin" is enabled.

Tries to automatically pick
the skin based on the
element's player name.
fancymenu.elements.player_entity.slim.de: If the skin should be slim.
fancymenu.elements.progress_bar.backgrou:
The background color is used in case there
is no background texture defined for the element.

If a background texture is defined,
the background color will be ignored.
fancymenu.elements.progress_bar.bar_colo:
The bar color is used in case there
is no bar texture defined for the element.
fancymenu.elements.progress_bar.bar_text:
If a bar texture is defined,
the bar color will be ignored.
fancymenu.elements.progress_bar.desc:
A customizable progress bar which
supports setting a custom text source
for the current progress.
fancymenu.elements.progress_bar.progress:
Use the current progress of this progress bar
as anchor origin position when using
this element as Element anchor.
That way other elements move with
the progress of the progress bar.
fancymenu.elements.progress_bar.source.d:
The progress source is the current progress
as percentage number between 0 and 100 or
floating point number between 0.0 and 1.0,
depending on the progress value mode.
The source supports placeholders, so there's
nothing that holds you from getting creative!
fancymenu.elements.shape.color.desc:
Set the HEX color of the shape.
Supports alpha channel (RGBA)!
fancymenu.elements.shape.rectangle.desc:
A rectangular shape.
Supports custom HEX RGBA colors.
fancymenu.elements.slider.desc:
A slider button.

Can be used to set variable
values by user input.
fancymenu.elements.slider.editor.list.se:
Set text values for the list slider.
One value per text line.
fancymenu.elements.slider.editor.set_lab:
The prefix of the slider label.

The base of the slider label
is always the current value.

The suffix of the slider label.

The base of the slider label
is always the current value.
fancymenu.elements.slider.editor.set_var:
Link this slider to a variable.
Use the variable name.

The variable can be a new
or an existing variable.
fancymenu.elements.slider.editor.type.de:
Set the type of this slider.

When using the list type,
you can set a list of
text values and switch through
them when moving the slider.

The range type allows you
to switch through a range
of numbers.
You can set a min and a max value
when using this type.
fancymenu.elements.slider.v2.desc:
A slider button that can be used to
set variable values and more.
Executes actions on value change.
fancymenu.elements.slider.v2.label: Slider Label
fancymenu.elements.slider.v2.label.desc:
The label of the slider.

To show the current slider value as part
of the label, use the $$value placeholder.
fancymenu.elements.slider.v2.manage_acti:
The actions this slider will execute
when its value gets changed.

You can get the slider's current value
by using the $$value placeholder in
action values or requirement values.
fancymenu.elements.slider.v2.pre_selecte:
This is the value that will be pre-selected
when the slider gets created, so make
sure this points to a variable or something
the slider sets.
If the slider sets a Minecraft option,
point this to the option value.
fancymenu.elements.slider.v2.type.list.s:
Set text values for the list slider.
One value per text line.
At least two values (lines) needed.
The decimal place to round the value to.
One (1) decimal place is one place
after the decimal point.

To not round the value, set it to -1.
The maximum value the range slider can reach.
The minimum value the range slider can reach.
fancymenu.elements.slideshow.desc:
A slideshow.
To learn more about slideshows,
visit docs.fancymenu.net!
fancymenu.elements.splash.refresh.desc:
Pick a new splash everytime the screen
is getting reloaded or opened.
fancymenu.elements.text.base_color.desc:
Set the base color for the text.
Use HEX color codes.
fancymenu.elements.text.desc:
Add a text to render in
your layout.

Choose between local and online
sources for the text content.
The color used for every second row when 'Alternate Row Colors' is enabled.

The padding inside table cells.
Higher values create more space between content and cell borders.
Customize the appearance of Markdown tables.

The margin around tables.
Adds space above and below each table.
If the element should parse Markdown formatting codes.
fancymenu.elements.text.scroll_grabber_c:
The color of the grabber.
Use HEX color codes.
fancymenu.elements.text.set_source.direc: Set direct text content to render.
fancymenu.elements.text.set_source.local: Use a TXT file as content.
fancymenu.elements.text.set_source.web.d:
Get the plain web text content
of a website as text.
fancymenu.elements.text.source_mode.desc:
Direct Text:
Directly input a text to render.

Local Source:
Use a TXT file as source.

Web Source:
Use the plain text content
of a website as source.

Changing the source mode will
reset the text content!

You can undo source changing
by pressing CTRL + Z!
fancymenu.elements.text.text_border.desc:
The text border is the space
between the text and the left
and right side of the element.
fancymenu.elements.text.v2.desc:
Renders a text body.
It support multi-line text, markdown
and has many options to customize
the look and feel of the element
and its content.
If this element should be interactable.
Disable this if you experience problems with
clicking elements above or under this text element.
fancymenu.elements.text.v2.source_mode.d:
Direct: Input text content via text editor.
Resource: Set a source file to get the text content from.
fancymenu.elements.ticker.async.desc:
If the ticker should run in
a separate thread (asynchronous).
fancymenu.elements.ticker.desc:
Allows you to execute actions
every tick.

Supports asynchronous ticking
and tick delays.

Can be set to tick only once
every time you open the screen.

This element is only visible
in the editor.
fancymenu.elements.ticker.manage_actions:
Manage the actions this ticker
should execute.
fancymenu.elements.ticker.tick_delay.des: Set the delay between ticks in milliseconds.
fancymenu.elements.ticker.tick_mode.desc:
Normal: Ticker ticks every tick.

Session: Ticker ticks once per game session.

On Load Screen: Ticker ticks once every time you load the screen.
Keep in mind that screens also get
reloaded when resizing the game window.
fancymenu.elements.tooltip.background_te:
Set a custom background texture.
Uses nine-slicing to resize the texture for the current tooltip size.
fancymenu.elements.tooltip.desc:
Renders a tooltip at a specific position or the mouse position.
Has full Markdown support, similar to Text elements.
Control its visibility with loading requirements.
fancymenu.elements.tooltip.mouse_followi: If the tooltip should follow the mouse when outside the editor.
fancymenu.elements.tooltip.nine_slice.de:
Here you can set settings related to the
nine-slicing logic of the custom tooltip background.
fancymenu.elements.vanilla_button.copy_l:
The widget locator points to a
specific widget in a specific screen.

The widget locator is used for actions like 'Mimic Button'.
fancymenu.elements.vanilla_button.copyri: You can't move the Copyright button out-of-screen!
fancymenu.elements.vanilla_button.draggi: To move this element, change its anchor point first!
fancymenu.elements.video_mcef.desc:
A video player powered by MCEF.
This element needs the MCEF mod to work!
fancymenu.elements.widgets.generic.navig:
If the user should be able to focus this
widget by using the Tab/Arrow key navigation.
fancymenu.fancymenu.editor.layoutoptions:
Add this layout to a group to randomly
pick one of the group's layouts
when opening the screen.

Can be used to randomize
backgrounds and other elements.

If layouts of this random group
should be random everytime the
screen gets opened or if only one layout
should be picked the first time
the screen gets opened.

Set the group of this layout.
One layout per group gets picked
when opening the screen.
fancymenu.game_intro.desc:
Plays an animated image or video before the
Title Screen is shown for the first time.
You can't edit the title of Custom GUIs.
To edit Custom GUI titles, edit the GUI in
the 'Manage Custom GUIs' screen.

Allows you to override the text at the
top of some screens with a custom one.

This option might not work for some screens.

The title needs to be at least 1 character long.
Spaces count as characters.
fancymenu.helper.editor.layoutoptions.ba:
Set an image, animation, panorama
or slideshow as background.
fancymenu.helper.editor.layoutoptions.un:
Add a screen to the blacklist
by its screen identifier.

Screens on the blacklist will
be ignored by the layout, so
the customizations don't get
applied to this screen.

You can get the identifier
of a screen by clicking on
Customization -> Copy Identifier of Current Screen
while in the screen.

Add a screen to the whitelist
by its screen identifier.

If there are screens on the
whitelist, only these screens
will be customized by the layout.
All other screens will be ignored!

You can get the identifier
of a screen by clicking on
Customization -> Copy Identifier of Current Screen
while in the screen.

Are you sure?

Do you really want to clear the blacklist?

Are you sure?

Do you really want to clear the whitelist?

Are you sure?

Do you really want to remove this identifier?

Are you sure?

Do you really want to remove this identifier?
fancymenu.helper.editor.properties.autos: Here you can set the base window size of your layout.
This should be the size your layout was designed for.
If you made it in the current window size, just leave the values like they are.

Let FancyMenu handle the scale
 of the screen, so your layout works
for every scale and resolution.

To do this, resize the window
until everything looks good and
elements are not too far apart
from each other and click on
this button.

This will make text look blurry
at some scales.
This can't be fixed and the best
workaround is to use images
with background as text elements.

You need to set a forced GUI scale
before you can use auto-scaling!

It's recommended to use 2 as
forced GUI scale.

To set a forced GUI scale,
right-click the editor background
and click on Force GUI Scale.
fancymenu.helper.editor.properties.scale:
Force a GUI scale for this screen.

Only overrides the scale for the
target screen, not for all screens!
fancymenu.layout.editor.edit_close_scree: This action script gets executed when closing the screen.
fancymenu.layout.editor.edit_open_screen: This action script gets executed when opening the screen.
fancymenu.layout.manage.delete.confirm:
Delete Layout?

Do you really want to delete this layout?

You can't undo this!
fancymenu.layout.manage.rename.error.emp:
Unable to rename layout!

The file name has to be at least one character long!
fancymenu.layout.manage.rename.error.fil:
Unable to rename layout!

A layout with the same name already exists!
fancymenu.layout_editor.grid.snapping.de: If elements should snap to the grid lines when being moved.
fancymenu.layout_editor.grid.snapping.st:
Controls how strongly elements snap to grid lines.
Lower values require more precision.
Higher values snap from further away.
fancymenu.listeners.manage.cancel_warnin:
Are you sure?

Do you really want to cancel?

This will undo everything you've done in here!
fancymenu.listeners.manage.desc:
Listeners are a very powerful feature that allows you
to execute an action script when specific things happen,
like when a user types on their keyboard, performs a mouse click
or even when things happen in worlds, like when the player dies.

Listeners aren't bound to screens, to they constantly
listen for events, even if there isn't a screen open at all,
like when playing in a singleplayer world or on a server.
fancymenu.listeners.manage.rename_tip: Rename listeners by double-clicking their display name.
fancymenu.listeners.manage.quick_edit_ti: Right-click listeners to quick-edit their actions.
fancymenu.listeners.manage.delete_warnin:
Are you sure?

Do you really want to delete this listener?

You can't undo this!
fancymenu.listeners.on_block_broke.desc:
This listener triggers once when the player breaks a block.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$block_key = The resource location of the broken block
- $$broke_with_item_key = The resource location of the item/tool that was used (or EMPTY when nothing was held)
- $$block_pos_x = The X coordinate of the broken block
- $$block_pos_y = The Y coordinate of the broken block
- $$block_pos_z = The Z coordinate of the broken block
fancymenu.listeners.on_block_placed.desc:
This listener triggers once when the player places a block.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$block_key = The resource location of the placed block
- $$block_pos_x = The X coordinate of the placed block
- $$block_pos_y = The Y coordinate of the placed block
- $$block_pos_z = The Z coordinate of the placed block
fancymenu.listeners.on_char_typed: On Keyboard Character Typed in Screen
fancymenu.listeners.on_char_typed.desc:
This listener triggers whenever a character is typed in a screen.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$char = The typed character
fancymenu.listeners.on_chat_message_rece:
Triggers whenever the client displays a normal player chat message.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$chat_message_string = Plain text version of the received chat line
- $$chat_message_component = Full component JSON of the received chat line
- $$sender_uuid = UUID of the sender (or ERROR if unavailable)
- $$sender_name = Plain name of the sender (or ERROR if unavailable)
fancymenu.listeners.on_chat_message_sent:
Triggers when the local player sends a chat message to the server.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$chat_message_string = Plain text version of the sent chat line
- $$chat_message_component = Full component JSON of the sent chat line
fancymenu.listeners.on_close_screen.desc:
Triggers right after a screen got closed.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$screen_identifier = Identifier of the screen that was closed
fancymenu.listeners.on_damage_taken.desc:
This listener triggers once when the player takes damage.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$damage_amount = The amount of health removed by the hit
- $$damage_type = The resource location of the damage type
- $$is_fatal_damage = TRUE when the hit reduced the player to zero health
- $$damage_source = The resource location of the entity that caused the damage or NONE when unavailable
fancymenu.listeners.on_death.desc:
Triggers right after the vanilla death screen opens for the local player.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$days_survived = In-game days survived (rounded down) since the last death
- $$death_reason_string = Plain text description of the death reason
- $$death_reason_component = Full component JSON of the death reason
- $$death_pos_x = X coordinate where the player died
- $$death_pos_y = Y coordinate where the player died
- $$death_pos_z = Z coordinate where the player died
fancymenu.listeners.on_dimension_entered:
This listener triggers once when the player enters a new dimension.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$dimension_key = The resource location of the entered dimension
fancymenu.listeners.on_effect_gained.des:
This listener triggers once when the player gains a status effect.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$effect_key = The resource location of the effect that was applied
- $$effect_type = The effect category (positive, negative, neutral)
- $$effect_duration = The effect duration in ticks remaining
fancymenu.listeners.on_effect_lost.desc:
This listener triggers once when the player loses a status effect.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$effect_key = The resource location of the effect that expired
- $$effect_type = The effect category (positive, negative, neutral)
fancymenu.listeners.on_enter_biome.desc:
This listener triggers once when the player enters a new biome.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$biome_key = The resource location of the biome the player entered
fancymenu.listeners.on_enter_structure.d:
Requires FancyMenu on the server.

This listener triggers once when the player enters a structure using coarse structure-area detection.

Because it considers the entire structure footprint, it can also fire when a structure is near or below the player (for example, a mineshaft beneath the surface).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$structure_key = The resource location of the structure the player entered
fancymenu.listeners.on_enter_structure.h:
Requires FancyMenu on the server.

This listener triggers once when the player actually steps into a structure's interior.

It uses high precision detection, so it only fires when the player enters the structure's bounding boxes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$structure_key = The resource location of the structure the player entered
fancymenu.listeners.on_entity_died.desc:
Requires FancyMenu on the server.

This listener triggers whenever an entity dies anywhere on the connected server/world (even if the player is far away or in another dimension).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$entity_key = The resource location of the entity type that died
- $$distance_to_player = The distance from the player to the death position (returns -1 when the entity died in another dimension)
- $$death_pos_x = The X coordinate where the entity died
- $$death_pos_y = The Y coordinate where the entity died
- $$death_pos_z = The Z coordinate where the entity died
- $$entity_uuid = The UUID of the entity that died
- $$dimension_key = The dimension the entity died in
- $$damage_type = The resource location of the damage type that caused the death
- $$is_same_dimension_as_player = If TRUE, the entity died in the same dimension as the player
- $$entity_killed_by_name = The plain text name of the killer or NONE when unavailable
- $$entity_killed_by_key = The resource location of the killer's type (uses minecraft:player for players, NONE when unavailable)
- $$entity_killed_by_uuid = The UUID of the killer or NONE when unavailable
fancymenu.listeners.on_entity_in_sight.d:
This listener triggers once when an entity first becomes visible in the player's field of view (and is not farther away than 200 blocks).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$entity_key = The resource location of the visible entity type
- $$distance_to_player = The distance from the player's eyes to the entity
- $$entity_pos_x = The entity's X coordinate
- $$entity_pos_y = The entity's Y coordinate
- $$entity_pos_z = The entity's Z coordinate
- $$entity_uuid = The UUID of the visible entity
fancymenu.listeners.on_entity_mounted.de:
This listener triggers once when the player begins riding an entity.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$entity_key = The resource location of the mounted entity type
- $$entity_pos_x = The entity's X coordinate when mounting started
- $$entity_pos_y = The entity's Y coordinate when mounting started
- $$entity_pos_z = The entity's Z coordinate when mounting started
- $$entity_uuid = The UUID of the mounted entity
fancymenu.listeners.on_entity_spawned.de:
Requires FancyMenu on the server.

This listener triggers whenever an entity spawns anywhere on the connected server/world (even if the player is far away or in another dimension).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$entity_key = The resource location of the spawned entity type
- $$distance_to_player = The distance from the player to the spawn location (returns -1 when the entity spawned in another dimension)
- $$entity_pos_x = The entity's X coordinate at spawn time
- $$entity_pos_y = The entity's Y coordinate at spawn time
- $$entity_pos_z = The entity's Z coordinate at spawn time
- $$entity_uuid = The UUID of the spawned entity
- $$dimension_key = The dimension the entity spawned in
- $$is_same_dimension_as_player = If TRUE, the entity spawned in the same dimension as the player
fancymenu.listeners.on_entity_starts_bei: On Entity Starts Being In Sight

This listener triggers once when an entity first becomes visible in the player's field of view (and is not farther away than 200 blocks).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$entity_key = The resource location of the visible entity type
- $$distance_to_player = The distance from the player's eyes to the entity
- $$entity_pos_x = The entity's X coordinate
- $$entity_pos_y = The entity's Y coordinate
- $$entity_pos_z = The entity's Z coordinate
- $$entity_uuid = The UUID of the visible entity
fancymenu.listeners.on_entity_stops_bein: On Entity Stops Being In Sight

This listener triggers once when an entity that was previously visible in the player's field of view stops being visible (or moves farther away than 200 blocks).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$entity_key = The resource location of the entity type that just left the view
- $$distance_to_player = The last measured distance from the player's eyes to the entity
- $$entity_pos_x = The entity's X coordinate
- $$entity_pos_y = The entity's Y coordinate
- $$entity_pos_z = The entity's Z coordinate
- $$entity_uuid = The UUID of the entity that just left the view
This listener triggers once when the player stops riding their current entity.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$entity_key = The resource location of the entity that was dismounted
- $$entity_pos_x = The entity's X coordinate when dismounting
- $$entity_pos_y = The entity's Y coordinate when dismounting
- $$entity_pos_z = The entity's Z coordinate when dismounting
- $$entity_uuid = The UUID of the entity that was dismounted
fancymenu.listeners.on_experience_change:
This listener triggers whenever the player's total experience amount changes (gaining or losing XP).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$new_experience_amount = The player's total experience value after the change
- $$old_experience_amount = The player's total experience value before the change
- $$is_level_up = TRUE when the change increased the player's level
fancymenu.listeners.on_file_downloaded.d:
This listener triggers when a file finishes downloading via the 'Download File to Game Directory' action.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$download_url = The URL of the file that got downloaded
- $$target_file_path = The path the file got saved to
- $$download_succeeded = If the file download was successful (true/false)
fancymenu.listeners.on_file_selected.des:
This listener triggers after the 'Select File' action finishes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$selected_file_path = The absolute path of the chosen file (empty when the dialog was cancelled)
- $$target_file_path = The resolved path inside the Minecraft instance that received the file
- $$selection_succeeded = 'true' when the file was copied successfully
- $$selection_cancelled = 'true' when the dialog was closed without selecting a file
- $$failure_reason = Error information when the action failed
fancymenu.listeners.on_fully_frozen.desc: This listener triggers once when the player becomes fully frozen.
fancymenu.listeners.on_interacted_with_b:
This listener triggers once when the player successfully interacts with a block.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$block_key = The resource location of the interacted block
- $$block_pos_x = The X coordinate of the block
- $$block_pos_y = The Y coordinate of the block
- $$block_pos_z = The Z coordinate of the block
fancymenu.listeners.on_interacted_with_e:
This listener triggers once when the player successfully interacts with an entity.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$entity_key = The resource location of the interacted entity type
- $$entity_pos_x = The entity's X coordinate at the time of interaction
- $$entity_pos_y = The entity's Y coordinate at the time of interaction
- $$entity_pos_z = The entity's Z coordinate at the time of interaction
- $$entity_uuid = The UUID of the interacted entity
fancymenu.listeners.on_item_broke.desc:
This listener triggers once when an item in the player's inventory breaks.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$item_key = The resource location of the broken item
- $$item_type = Category of the broken item (tool, armor, other)
fancymenu.listeners.on_item_consumed.des:
This listener triggers once when the player finishes consuming an item.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$item_key = The resource location of the item that was consumed
fancymenu.listeners.on_item_dropped.desc:
This listener triggers once when the player drops an item from their inventory.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$item_key = The resource location of the item that was dropped
fancymenu.listeners.on_item_picked_up.de:
This listener triggers once when the player picks up an item entity.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$item_key = The resource location of the item that was picked up
fancymenu.listeners.on_item_used.desc:
This listener triggers once when the player uses an item.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$item_key = The resource location of the item that was used
- $$used_on_type = The interaction context (block, entity, self, none)
- $$used_on_entity_key = The resource location of the entity type that was targeted, empty when none
- $$used_on_block_key = The resource location of the block that was targeted, empty when none
- $$target_pos_x = Target X position when available, otherwise -1
- $$target_pos_y = Target Y position when available, otherwise -1
- $$target_pos_z = Target Z position when available, otherwise -1
fancymenu.listeners.on_jump.desc: This listener triggers once whenever the local player performs a jump action.
fancymenu.listeners.on_key_pressed.desc:
This listener triggers whenever a keyboard key is pressed, which works both while a screen is open and when in-game (in a world/server). The listener keeps firing while the key is held down and the screen continues to receive repeat events.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$key_name = The resolved display name of the key
- $$key_keycode = The GLFW key code
- $$key_scancode = The GLFW scan code
- $$key_modifiers = The active modifier bit mask
fancymenu.listeners.on_key_released.desc:
This listener triggers whenever a keyboard key is released, which works both while a screen is open and when in-game (in a world/server).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$key_name = The resolved display name of the key
- $$key_keycode = The GLFW key code
- $$key_scancode = The GLFW scan code
- $$key_modifiers = The active modifier bit mask
fancymenu.listeners.on_leave_biome.desc:
This listener triggers once when the player leaves their current biome.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$biome_key = The resource location of the biome the player just left
fancymenu.listeners.on_leave_structure.d:
Requires FancyMenu on the server.

This listener triggers once when the player leaves their current structure using coarse structure-area detection.

Because it considers the entire structure footprint, it can also fire when a structure is near or below the player (for example, a mineshaft beneath the surface).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$structure_key = The resource location of the structure the player just left
fancymenu.listeners.on_leave_structure.h:
Requires FancyMenu on the server.

This listener triggers once when the player leaves the interior of their current structure.

It uses high precision detection, so it only fires after the player fully exits the structure's bounding boxes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$structure_key = The resource location of the structure the player just left
This listener triggers once when the crosshair starts pointing at a block in the world.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$block_key = The resource location of the targeted block
- $$distance = The distance from the player's eyes to the block hit position
fancymenu.listeners.on_mouse_button_clic:
This listener triggers once when a mouse button is pressed, which works both while a screen is open and when in-game (in a world/server).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$button = Which button was pressed (left, right, middle)
- $$mouse_pos_x = The current mouse X position
- $$mouse_pos_y = The current mouse Y position
fancymenu.listeners.on_mouse_button_rele:
This listener triggers once when a mouse button is released, which works both while a screen is open and when in-game (in a world/server).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$button = Which button was released (left, right, middle)
- $$mouse_pos_x = The current mouse X position
- $$mouse_pos_y = The current mouse Y position
fancymenu.listeners.on_mouse_moved.desc:
This listener triggers whenever the mouse cursor moves while a screen is open.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$mouse_pos_x = The current mouse X position
- $$mouse_pos_y = The current mouse Y position
- $$mouse_move_delta_x = The horizontal distance moved since the last event
- $$mouse_move_delta_y = The vertical distance moved since the last event
fancymenu.listeners.on_mouse_scrolled.de:
This listener triggers whenever the mouse wheel is scrolled while a screen is open.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$scroll_delta_y = The vertical scroll amount for the event
fancymenu.listeners.on_music_track_start:
This listener triggers once when a new music track starts playing.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$track_resource_location = The resolved resource location of the audio file that started
- $$track_display_name = Human-readable track name when available, otherwise UNKNOWN
- $$track_artist = Reported track artist when available, otherwise UNKNOWN
- $$track_duration_ms = Track duration expressed in milliseconds (0 when unknown)
fancymenu.listeners.on_music_track_stopp:
This listener triggers once when the current music track stops playing (naturally or because it was replaced).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$track_resource_location = The resolved resource location of the audio file that stopped
- $$track_display_name = Human-readable track name when available, otherwise UNKNOWN
- $$track_artist = Reported track artist when available, otherwise UNKNOWN
- $$track_duration_ms = Track duration expressed in milliseconds (0 when unknown)
fancymenu.listeners.on_open_screen.desc:
Triggers immediately after a screen becomes active, allowing actions such as "Open Screen or Custom GUI" to override it.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$screen_identifier = Identifier of the screen that just opened
fancymenu.listeners.on_other_player_died:
Triggers when another player in the current world dies.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$player_name = The plain name of the player who died
- $$player_uuid = The UUID of the player who died
- $$death_pos_x = X coordinate where the player died
- $$death_pos_y = Y coordinate where the player died
- $$death_pos_z = Z coordinate where the player died
fancymenu.listeners.on_other_player_join:
Triggers when another player joins the current world or connected server.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$player_name = The plain name of the player who joined
- $$player_uuid = The UUID of the player who joined
fancymenu.listeners.on_other_player_left:
Triggers when another player leaves the current world or connected server.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$player_name = The plain name of the player who left
- $$player_uuid = The UUID of the player who left
This listener triggers once whenever the local player's block position changes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $old_pos_x = Previous block X coordinate
- $old_pos_y = Previous block Y coordinate
- $old_pos_z = Previous block Z coordinate
- $new_pos_x = New block X coordinate
- $new_pos_y = New block Y coordinate
- $new_pos_z = New block Z coordinate
fancymenu.listeners.on_quit_minecraft.de:
This listener triggers once when the Minecraft client begins shutting down.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$timestamp_millis = Epoch milliseconds when the quit event fired
- $$timestamp_iso = ISO-8601 timestamp representing the quit moment
fancymenu.listeners.on_server_joined.des:
Triggers after the client finishes joining a multiplayer server.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$server_ip = IP address of the server the player joined
fancymenu.listeners.on_server_left.desc:
Triggers after the client disconnects from a multiplayer server.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$server_ip = IP address of the server the player left
fancymenu.listeners.on_start_looking_at_:
This listener triggers once when the crosshair starts pointing at a block in the world.

It only detects blocks within a maximum distance of 20 blocks from the player's eyes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$block_key = The resource location of the targeted block
- $$block_pos_x = The X coordinate of the targeted block
- $$block_pos_y = The Y coordinate of the targeted block
- $$block_pos_z = The Z coordinate of the targeted block
- $$distance_to_player = The distance from the player's eyes to the block hit position

This listener triggers once when the crosshair starts pointing at an entity.

It only detects entities within a maximum distance of 20 blocks from the player's eyes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$entity_key = The resource location of the targeted entity type
- $$distance_to_player = The distance from the player's eyes to the entity hit position
- $$entity_pos_x = The entity's X coordinate
- $$entity_pos_y = The entity's Y coordinate
- $$entity_pos_z = The entity's Z coordinate
- $$entity_uuid = The UUID of the targeted entity
fancymenu.listeners.on_start_swimming.de:
This listener triggers once when the player starts swimming.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$fluid_type = The resource location of the fluid the player started swimming in
fancymenu.listeners.on_start_touching_fl:
This listener triggers once when the player starts touching a fluid.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$fluid_type = The resource location of the fluid the player touched
fancymenu.listeners.on_started_burning.d: This listener triggers once when the player starts burning.
This listener triggers once when the player begins taking drowning damage.
This listener triggers once when the player starts freezing.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$freezing_intensity = The current freezing intensity (0.0 = no freeze, 1.0 = fully frozen)
fancymenu.listeners.on_started_running.d: This listener triggers once when the player starts sprinting.
fancymenu.listeners.on_stepping_on_block:
This listener triggers once when the player steps onto a block.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$block_key = The resource location of the block that was stepped on
- $$block_pos_x = The X coordinate of the block
- $$block_pos_y = The Y coordinate of the block
- $$block_pos_z = The Z coordinate of the block
fancymenu.listeners.on_stop_looking_at_b:
This listener triggers once when the crosshair stops pointing at a block and reports information about the block that was previously targeted.

It only reports data for blocks that were within a maximum distance of 20 blocks from the player's eyes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$block_key = The resource location of the block that was targeted
- $$block_pos_x = The X coordinate of the previously targeted block
- $$block_pos_y = The Y coordinate of the previously targeted block
- $$block_pos_z = The Z coordinate of the previously targeted block
- $$distance_to_player = The last measured distance from the player's eyes to the block hit position
fancymenu.listeners.on_stop_looking_at_e:
This listener triggers once when the crosshair stops pointing at an entity and fires with information about the entity that was previously targeted.

It reports data for entities that were within a maximum distance of 20 blocks from the player's eyes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$entity_key = The resource location of the entity type that was targeted
- $$distance_to_player = The last measured distance from the player's eyes to the entity hit position
- $$entity_pos_x = The entity's X coordinate
- $$entity_pos_y = The entity's Y coordinate
- $$entity_pos_z = The entity's Z coordinate
- $$entity_uuid = The UUID of the entity that was targeted
fancymenu.listeners.on_stop_swimming.des:
This listener triggers once when the player stops swimming.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$fluid_type = The resource location of the fluid the player stopped swimming in
fancymenu.listeners.on_stop_touching_flu:
This listener triggers once when the player stops touching a fluid.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$fluid_type = The resource location of the fluid the player stopped touching
fancymenu.listeners.on_stopped_burning.d: This listener triggers once when the player stops burning.
This listener triggers once when the player stops freezing.
fancymenu.listeners.on_stopped_running.d: This listener triggers once when the player stops sprinting.
This listener triggers whenever a FancyMenu variable gets updated/set.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$var_name = The variable name
- $$old_value = The old variable value
- $$new_value = The new variable value
fancymenu.listeners.on_weather_changed.d:
This listener triggers once whenever the weather state changes (clear, rain, or thunder).
It will also re-trigger when the local weather changes, which means if it is raining, for example, and you enter a biome that has no rain (desert) or a biome where it is snowing, the listener will re-trigger even though the global weather didn't change.
Entering a building also counts as local weather change while it is raining outside, because well, it doesn't rain inside.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$weather_type = The new global weather type (clear, rain, thunder)
- $$weather_can_snow = TRUE when precipitation at the player renders as snow
- $$weather_can_rain = TRUE when precipitation at the player renders as rain
fancymenu.listeners.on_world_entered.des:
Triggers after a singleplayer world finishes loading and the player regains control.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$world_name = Display name of the world
- $$world_save_path = Absolute path to the world save folder
- $$world_difficulty = Current game difficulty key
- $$world_cheats_allowed = TRUE when cheats are enabled
- $$world_icon_path = Absolute path to the world icon
- $$world_is_first_join = TRUE when this is the very first visit after creation
fancymenu.listeners.on_world_left.desc:
Triggers after a singleplayer world closes and finishes saving.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$world_name = Display name of the world
- $$world_save_path = Absolute path to the world save folder
- $$world_difficulty = Last known game difficulty key
- $$world_cheats_allowed = TRUE when cheats were enabled
- $$world_icon_path = Absolute path to the world icon
fancymenu.listeners.on_world_sound_trigg:
This listener triggers whenever a positional world sound starts playing near the player.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- $$sound_resource_location = The resolved resource location of the sound file that started
- $$sound_display_name = The localized display name shown in the subtitles overlay when available
- $$sound_origin_pos_x = The X position of the sound's origin
- $$sound_origin_pos_y = The Y position of the sound's origin
- $$sound_origin_pos_z = The Z position of the sound's origin
- $$sound_origin_distance_to_player = The distance between the player and the sound origin
- $$sound_origin_direction_from_player = Direction in degrees (0-360) relative to where the player is facing when the sound started

fancymenu.placeholders.audio_duration.de:
Returns the total duration of the current track
playing in an Audio element in MM:SS format (e.g. '03:45').
Returns '00:00' if no audio is playing.

Required values:
- element_identifier: The ID of the audio element to get the duration from
fancymenu.placeholders.audio_element_cur:
Gets the filename or display name of the currently playing track in an Audio element.
Returns "---" when no track is playing.
Takes the element identifier of the target Audio element.
Optionally takes display name mappings to show custom names for tracks.
Mapping format: track1.ogg=>Cool Name%%:%%track2.wav=>Another Name
fancymenu.placeholders.audio_element_vol:
Returns the volume of an Audio element
as a value between 0.0 (0%%) and 1.0 (100%%).
Takes the element identifier of the target Audio element.
fancymenu.placeholders.audio_playing_sta:
Returns the current playing state of an Audio element.
Use 'element_identifier' to specify the Audio element.
Returns 'true' if the audio is playing, 'false' if paused or stopped.
fancymenu.placeholders.audio_playtime.de:
Returns either the current play time of an Audio element
(MM:SS format) or the play progress percentage (0-100).
Returns '00:00' or '0' if no audio is playing.

Required values:
- element_identifier: The ID of the audio element
- show_percentage: Set to 'true' to show percentage instead of time
fancymenu.placeholders.calc.desc:
